We do not say more perfect or most unique in careful writing, though advertisements do. The examination usually rewards the careful form: perfect, not more perfect; unique, not most unique. A related trap is the word preferable, which already means more desirable, so preferable than is wrong and preferable to is right.

The comparative is often used in a construction with the, as in the more you read, the more you learn. Here the two comparatives are balanced, and the sentence is correct only when both halves follow the same pattern. Another fixed pattern is the comparative with than any other, used for the superlative idea: Rina is taller than any other girl in the class. The word other is essential, because without it the sentence compares Rina with herself and becomes illogical.

The superlative is usually used with the definite article: the best, the tallest, the most beautiful. When the superlative is used as a predicate and no comparison is intended, the article is often dropped: This is best. When a possessive comes before the superlative, the article is dropped as well: her best friend, not her the best friend. A candidate should watch these small omissions, because the error-spotting question often turns on a missing or an extra the.

Comparatives can be made stronger or weaker with modifiers. Much, far, a lot and rather go with the comparative: much better, far more useful, rather taller. Very goes with the positive degree, not with the comparative: very good, but not very better. Even, still and no are also used with comparatives: even better, still worse, no more than. The pair very and much is a favourite of the paper, and the rule is simple: very with the positive, much with the comparative.

When two qualities of the same person or thing are compared, the adjective takes more rather than er: She is more wise than clever, not wiser than clever. The reason is that the comparison is between qualities, not between two separate people. A similar rule applies to two qualities of the same object: The box is more long than wide. This construction is less common but it appears in the bank, and the safe habit is to use more when the two adjectives describe the same subject.

The positive degree is also used for equality and inequality. Equality takes as ... as: Rina is as tall as Mina. Inequality takes not so ... as or not as ... as: Rina is not so tall as Mina. In these patterns the adjective stays in the positive degree, and the error to watch is a comparative slipped in after as, as in as taller as. The pair as ... as is fixed, and nothing goes between the two as except the adjective.

The comparative of inferiority uses less and least: This book is less useful than that one; This is the least useful book of the three. Less is the opposite of more, and least is the opposite of most. A common error is to write lesser than for two things; lesser is an adjective meaning smaller in importance, and it is not the ordinary comparative of little. For countable nouns, fewer is used instead of less: fewer books, not less books.

The verb prefer has its own pattern. We say prefer A to B, not prefer A than B: She prefers tea to coffee. When the comparison is between two actions, the pattern is prefer doing A to doing B, or prefer to do A rather than do B. The word than appears only with rather, never directly after prefer. A question that offers prefer than is testing exactly this point.

The words elder and eldest are used only for members of a family and only before a noun: my elder brother, the eldest son. They are not used with than, so we do not say He is elder than me; the correct form is He is older than me. Older and oldest are the general forms and can be used for people, things and places. This distinction is small but it is asked, and it is easy to remember because elder stays inside the family.

A superlative inside the phrase one of the takes a plural noun: She is one of the best students in the class, not one of the best student. The reason is that she is one member of a group of best students, so the noun after of the must be plural. The verb that follows one of the is usually singular, because the subject is one: One of the best students is absent. Both halves of this pattern are tested together.

Adverbs follow the same three degrees as adjectives, but they take more and most rather than er and est, except for a few short forms. We say more carefully and most carefully, more fluently and most fluently. Short adverbs such as fast, hard, early and late take er and est: faster, fastest; harder, hardest; earlier, earliest. The adverb well has the irregular forms better and best, and badly has worse and worst. A sentence such as She sings more better is wrong twice, once for the double comparative and once for the wrong form of well.
Two things take the comparative with than; three or more take the superlative with the.
Never use more or most together with er or est.
One-syllable adjectives take er and est; long adjectives take more and most.
Good, bad, far, little, many and much are irregular and must be memorised.
Absolute adjectives such as perfect and unique are not compared.
Very goes with the positive degree; much goes with the comparative.
Use than any other, not than any, for the superlative idea.

She is the taller of the two sisters. Here two sisters are compared, so the comparative taller is correct, and of the two is the right phrase. The definite article the is used because the comparison is definite. If the sentence said of the three sisters, the correct form would be the tallest of the three.

This is the most unique building in the town. The sentence is wrong because unique already means one of a kind and cannot take most. The correct sentence is This is the unique building in the town, or, more naturally, This building is unique in the town.

He is more wiser than his brother. The double comparative more wiser is wrong. The correct form is He is wiser than his brother. If the adjective were intelligent, the correct form would be He is more intelligent than his brother, because intelligent takes more and not er.

Of all the boys, Rahul is the best. Here three or more boys are compared, so the superlative best is correct, and the definite article the is required. If only two boys were compared, the sentence would be Rahul is the better of the two.
Using a comparative for three or more things.
Writing more better or most tallest.
Using very with a comparative instead of much.
Comparing an absolute adjective such as perfect or unique.

Count the things being compared before you choose the degree. If the count is two, use the comparative and than; if it is three or more, use the superlative and the. That single check settles most questions on this topic.
as: তুলনামূলক স্তৰ (degrees of comparison) ইংৰাজী ব্যাকৰণৰ সেই অংশ, য'ত বিশেষণ বা ক্ৰিয়া-বিশেষণে দুই বা ততোধিক বস্তুৰ তুলনা কৰোঁতে যি ৰূপ লয় তাক আলোচনা কৰা হয়। ধনাত্মক স্তৰে কেৱল এটা গুণ কয়, যেনে ৰিনা ওখ। তুলনামূলক স্তৰে দুজন ব্যক্তি বা দুটা বস্তুৰ তুলনা কৰে, যেনে ৰিনা মিনাতকৈ ওখ। অতিশয় স্তৰে তিনিজন বা ততোধিকৰ তুলনা কৰে, যেনে ৰিনা শ্ৰেণীৰ আটাইতকৈ ওখ ছোৱালী। DHS আৰু DME কাৰিকৰী গ্ৰেড III পত্ৰত এই বিষয়টো সাধাৰণতে তালিকা পূৰণ হিচাপে নহয়, বাক্য শুধৰণি, ভুল নিৰ্ণয় আৰু ৰিক্ত স্থান পূৰণত আহে, য'ত তিনিটা শুদ্ধ শব্দৰ মাজত এটা ভুল স্তৰ ৰখা হয়।

প্ৰথমে তুলনা কৰা বস্তুৰ সংখ্যা ঠিক কৰিব লাগে। তুলনামূলক স্তৰে ঠিক দুটাক লয় আৰু তাৰ পিছত than আহে। অতিশয় স্তৰে তিনিটা বা ততোধিকক লয় আৰু তাৰ আগত the আহে। ৰিনা তিনি ছোৱালীৰ ওখতৰ বাক্যটো দুবাৰ ভুল: taller তুলনামূলক স্তৰ তিনিজনৰ বাবে ব্যৱহাৰ হৈছে, আৰু of the three ৰ লগত tallest হ'ব লাগিছিল। ৰিনা মিনাতকৈ tallest বাক্যটোও ভুল, কাৰণ অতিশয় স্তৰৰ লগত than নাহে। এই দুটা ভুলেই এই বিষয়ৰ বহু প্ৰশ্নৰ মূল।

বেছিভাগ এক-অক্ষৰ বিশেষণে er যোগ কৰি তুলনামূলক আৰু est যোগ কৰি অতিশয় স্তৰ গঠন কৰে: tall, taller, tallest; small, smaller, smallest; bright, brighter, brightest। y ৰে শেষ হোৱা দুই-অক্ষৰ বিশেষণে y ক i লৈ সলাই ending যোগ কৰে: happy, happier, happiest; easy, easier, easiest; busy, busier, busiest। স্বৰধ্বনি বা l ৰে শেষ হোৱা কিছুমান দুই-অক্ষৰ বিশেষণেও ending লয়: narrow, narrower, narrowest; simple, simpler, simplest। বানানৰ নিয়ম মন কৰিব লাগে, কাৰণ ভুল বানৰ তুলনামূলক ৰূপ এটা সাধাৰণ বিভ্ৰান্তিকৰ বিকল্প।

দীঘল বিশেষণে ending নলয়; সিহঁতে more আৰু most লয়: beautiful, more beautiful, most beautiful; difficult, more difficult, most difficult; intelligent, more intelligent, most intelligent। সাধাৰণ ভুল হৈছে ending আৰু more দুয়োটা ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা, যেনে more better বা most tallest। এই দ্বৈত তুলনামূলক সদায় ভুল। এটা সহজ পৰীক্ষা: বিশেষণটোৰ এটাতকৈ বেছি অক্ষৰ আছে নেকি আৰু y ৰে শেষ নহয় নেকি চাওক; তেন্তে সেয়া more আৰু most লয়, er আৰু est নহয়।

কিছুমান বিশেষণ অপৰিৱৰ্তনীয় আৰু মনত ৰাখিব লাগে। Good ৰ better আৰু best; bad ৰ worse আৰু worst; far ৰ farther বা further আৰু farthest বা furthest; little ৰ less আৰু least; many আৰু much ৰ more আৰু most; old ৰ older আৰু oldest, যদিও পৰিয়ালৰ সদস্যৰ বাবে elder আৰু eldest ব্যৱহাৰ হয়। Late ৰ সময়ৰ বাবে later আৰু latest, কিন্তু ক্ৰমৰ বাবে latter আৰু last। এই যোৰবোৰ প্ৰত্যক্ষভাৱে সোধা হয়, আৰু যি প্ৰাৰ্থীয়ে জানে তেওঁ সহজ নম্বৰ পায়।

কিছুমান বিশেষণ তুলনা কৰিব নোৱাৰি, কাৰণ সিহঁতে ইতিমধ্যে চূড়ান্ত অৱস্থা বুজায়। Dead, unique, perfect, complete, full, empty, eternal আৰু universal এই গোটত পৰে। যতনশীল লিখাত আমি more perfect বা most unique নিলিখোঁ, যদিও বিজ্ঞাপনে লিখে। পৰীক্ষাই সাধাৰণতে যতনশীল ৰূপক পুৰস্কৃত কৰে: perfect, more perfect নহয়; unique, most unique নহয়। ইয়াৰ লগত জড়িত এটা ফান্দ হৈছে preferable, যাৰ অৰ্থ ইতিমধ্যে অধিক ইচ্ছনীয়, গতিকে preferable than ভুল আৰু preferable to শুদ্ধ।

তুলনামূলক স্তৰ প্ৰায়ে the ৰ সৈতে এটা গঠনত আহে, যেনে the more you read, the more you learn। ইয়াত দুটা তুলনামূলক স্তৰ ভাৰসাম্যত থাকে, আৰু বাক্যটো তেতিয়াহে শুদ্ধ যেতিয়া দুয়ো অৰ্ধ একেই আৰ্হি অনুসৰণ কৰে। আন এটা নিৰ্দিষ্ট আৰ্হি হৈছে than any other, যি অতিশয় স্তৰৰ ভাৱ দিয়ে: ৰিনা শ্ৰেণীৰ আন যিকোনো ছোৱালীতকৈ ওখ। other শব্দটো অত্যাৱশ্যক, কাৰণ ইয়াৰ অবিহনে বাক্যই ৰিনাক নিজৰ সৈতে তুলনা কৰি অসংগত কৰি তোলে।

অতিশয় স্তৰ সাধাৰণতে নিৰ্দিষ্ট article ৰ সৈতে ব্যৱহাৰ হয়: the best, the tallest, the most beautiful। যেতিয়া অতিশয় স্তৰ predicate হিচাপে ব্যৱহাৰ হয় আৰু কোনো তুলনা অভিপ্ৰায় নাথাকে, article প্ৰায়ে বাদ দিয়া হয়: This is best। যেতিয়া অতিশয় স্তৰৰ আগত possessive আহে, article বাদ দিয়া হয়: her best friend, her the best friend নহয়। প্ৰাৰ্থীয়ে এই সৰু বাদ-যোগ মন কৰিব লাগে, কাৰণ ভুল নিৰ্ণয়ৰ প্ৰশ্ন প্ৰায়ে এটা বাদ পৰা বা বেছি the ৰ ওপৰত ঘূৰে।

তুলনামূলক স্তৰক much, far, a lot, rather আদিৰে বঢ়াব বা কমাব পাৰি: much better, far more useful, rather taller। Very ধনাত্মক স্তৰৰ লগত আহে, তুলনামূলক স্তৰৰ লগত নহয়: very good, কিন্তু very better নহয়। Even, still আৰু noও তুলনামূলক স্তৰৰ লগত আহে: even better, still worse, no more than। very আৰু much ৰ যোৰ পত্ৰৰ প্ৰিয়, আৰু নিয়মটো সহজ: very ধনাত্মকৰ লগত, much তুলনামূলকৰ লগত।

যেতিয়া এজন ব্যক্তি বা এটা বস্তুৰ দুটা গুণৰ তুলনা কৰা হয়, বিশেষণে er নহয় more লয়: She is more wise than clever, wiser than clever নহয়। কাৰণ তুলনাটো দুজন পৃথক ব্যক্তিৰ মাজত নহয়, দুটা গুণৰ মাজত। একেই নিয়ম এটা বস্তুৰ দুটা গুণৰ বাবেও প্ৰযোজ্য: The box is more long than wide। এই গঠন কম সচৰাচৰ, কিন্তু প্ৰশ্নগোটত আহে, আৰু নিৰাপদ অভ্যাস হৈছে দুয়ো বিশেষণে একেই কৰ্তাক বৰ্ণনা কৰিলে more ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা।

ধনাত্মক স্তৰ সমতা আৰু অসামতাতো ব্যৱহাৰ হয়। সমতাই as ... as লয়: ৰিনা মিনাৰ দৰেই ওখ। অসামতাই not so ... as বা not as ... as লয়: ৰিনা মিনাৰ দৰে ওখ নহয়। এই আৰ্হিত বিশেষণ ধনাত্মক স্তৰতে থাকে, আৰু চাবলগীয়া ভুলটো হৈছে as ৰ পিছত তুলনামূলক স্তৰ সুমুৱাই দিয়া, যেনে as taller as। as ... as যোৰ নিৰ্দিষ্ট, আৰু দুয়ো as ৰ মাজত বিশেষণৰ বাহিৰে আন একো নাহে।

হীনতাবাচক তুলনাই less আৰু least লয়: এই কিতাপখন সেইখনতকৈ কম উপযোগী; এইখন তিনিখনৰ ভিতৰত আটাইতকৈ কম উপযোগী। Less হৈছে more ৰ বিপৰীত, আৰু least হৈছে most ৰ বিপৰীত। এটা সাধাৰণ ভুল হৈছে দুটা বস্তুৰ বাবে lesser than লিখা; lesser মানে গুৰুত্বত সৰু, আৰু সেয়া little ৰ সাধাৰণ তুলনামূলক ৰূপ নহয়। গণনাযোগ্য বিশেষ্যৰ বাবে less ৰ সলনি fewer ব্যৱহাৰ হয়: fewer books, less books নহয়।

Prefer ক্ৰিয়াৰ নিজৰ এটা নিৰ্দিষ্ট আৰ্হি আছে। আমি prefer A to B লিখোঁ, prefer A than B নহয়: তাই চাহতকৈ কফি বেছি ভাল পায়। তুলনা দুটা কামৰ মাজত হ'লে আৰ্হিটো prefer doing A to doing B, বা prefer to do A rather than do B। than শব্দটো কেৱল rather ৰ লগত আহে, prefer ৰ পিছত প্ৰত্যক্ষভাৱে কেতিয়াও নাহে। prefer than দিয়া প্ৰশ্নই ঠিক এই কথাটোৱেই পৰীক্ষা কৰে।

Elder আৰু eldest কেৱল পৰিয়ালৰ সদস্যৰ বাবে আৰু কেৱল বিশেষ্যৰ আগত ব্যৱহাৰ হয়: মোৰ ডাঙৰ ভাই, ডাঙৰ পুত্ৰ। ইহঁত than ৰ লগত নাহে, গতিকে He is elder than me নহয়; শুদ্ধ ৰূপ He is older than me। Older আৰু oldest সাধাৰণ ৰূপ আৰু মানুহ, বস্তু আৰু ঠাইৰ বাবে ব্যৱহাৰ কৰিব পাৰি। এই পাৰ্থক্যটো সৰু কিন্তু সোধা হয়, আৰু মনত ৰখা সহজ কাৰণ elder পৰিয়ালৰ ভিতৰতেই থাকে।

one of the ৰ ভিতৰত থকা অতিশয় স্তৰে বহুবচন বিশেষ্য লয়: তাই শ্ৰেণীৰ আটাইতকৈ ভাল ছাত্ৰীসকলৰ এজনী, one of the best student নহয়। কাৰণ তাই আটাইতকৈ ভাল ছাত্ৰীসকলৰ এটা গোটৰ এজনী সদস্য, গতিকে of the ৰ পিছত বিশেষ্য বহুবচন হ'ব লাগে। one of the ৰ পিছত অহা ক্ৰিয়া সাধাৰণতে একবচন, কাৰণ কৰ্তা one: One of the best students is absent। এই আৰ্হিৰ দুয়ো অৰ্ধ একেলগে সোধা হয়।

ক্ৰিয়া-বিশেষণেও বিশেষণৰ দৰেই তিনি স্তৰ অনুসৰণ কৰে, কিন্তু কিছুমান চুটি ৰূপৰ বাহিৰে সিহঁতে er আৰু est ৰ সলনি more আৰু most লয়। আমি more carefully আৰু most carefully, more fluently আৰু most fluently লিখোঁ। fast, hard, early, late যেনে চুটি ক্ৰিয়া-বিশেষণে er আৰু est লয়: faster, fastest; harder, hardest; earlier, earliest। well ৰ অপৰিৱৰ্তনীয় ৰূপ better আৰু best, আৰু badly ৰ worse আৰু worst। She sings more better বাক্যটো দুবাৰ ভুল, এবাৰ দ্বৈত তুলনামূলকৰ বাবে আৰু এবাৰ well ৰ ভুল ৰূপৰ বাবে।
দুটা বস্তুৰ বাবে তুলনামূলক স্তৰ আৰু than; তিনি বা ততোধিকৰ বাবে অতিশয় স্তৰ আৰু the।
more বা most ৰ লগত er বা est কেতিয়াও নিদিব।
এক-অক্ষৰ বিশেষণে er আৰু est লয়; দীঘল বিশেষণে more আৰু most লয়।
good, bad, far, little, many, much অপৰিৱৰ্তনীয়, মনত ৰাখিব।
perfect, unique আদি চূড়ান্ত বিশেষণ তুলনা কৰিব নোৱাৰি।
very ধনাত্মক স্তৰৰ লগত, much তুলনামূলক স্তৰৰ লগত।
অতিশয় স্তৰৰ ভাৱৰ বাবে than any other, than any নহয়।

She is the taller of the two sisters। ইয়াত দুজনী ভনীয়েকৰ তুলনা হৈছে, গতিকে taller শুদ্ধ, আৰু of the two শুদ্ধ বাক্যাংশ। তুলনা নিৰ্দিষ্ট হোৱাৰ বাবে the ব্যৱহাৰ হৈছে। যদি of the three sisters হ'লহেঁতেন, তেন্তে the tallest of the three শুদ্ধ হ'লহেঁতেন।

This is the most unique building in the town। বাক্যটো ভুল, কাৰণ unique ৰ অৰ্থ ইতিমধ্যে এটাই-একক আৰু তাৰ লগত most নাহে। শুদ্ধ বাক্য This is the unique building in the town, বা অধিক স্বাভাৱিকভাৱে This building is unique in the town।

He is more wiser than his brother। more wiser দ্বৈত তুলনামূলক, গতিকে ভুল। শুদ্ধ ৰূপ He is wiser than his brother। যদি বিশেষণটো intelligent হ'লহেঁতেন, তেন্তে He is more intelligent than his brother শুদ্ধ হ'লহেঁতেন, কাৰণ intelligent এ more লয়, er নহয়।

Of all the boys, Rahul is the best। ইয়াত তিনি বা ততোধিক ল'ৰাৰ তুলনা হৈছে, গতিকে best অতিশয় স্তৰ শুদ্ধ, আৰু the অত্যাৱশ্যক। যদি কেৱল দুজন ল'ৰাৰ তুলনা হ'লহেঁতেন, তেন্তে Rahul is the better of the two হ'লহেঁতেন।
তিনি বা ততোধিকৰ বাবে তুলনামূলক স্তৰ ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা।
more better বা most tallest লিখা।
অতিশয় স্তৰৰ লগত than ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা।
অতিশয় স্তৰৰ আগত the পাহৰি যোৱা।
তুলনামূলক স্তৰৰ লগত very ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা, much ৰ সলনি।
perfect বা unique যেনে চূড়ান্ত বিশেষণ তুলনা কৰা।
স্তৰ বাছনি কৰাৰ আগতে তুলনা কৰা বস্তুৰ সংখ্যা গণনা কৰক। সংখ্যা দুটা হ'লে তুলনামূলক স্তৰ আৰু than; তিনি বা ততোধিক হ'লে অতিশয় স্তৰ আৰু the। এই এটা পৰীক্ষাই এই বিষয়ৰ বেছিভাগ প্ৰশ্নৰ উত্তৰ ঠিক কৰে।

en: Question tags: the shape of the sentence

A question tag is the short question added at the end of a statement, as in You are coming, aren't you? The tag turns a statement into a request for confirmation, and it is one of the easiest places in the paper to lose a mark because the rule has several small parts. The tag is built from two pieces: the auxiliary verb of the statement and a pronoun that stands for the subject. If the statement has no auxiliary, the tag uses do, does or did, and the main verb goes back to its base form.

The polarity rule is the first thing to apply. A positive statement takes a negative tag, and a negative statement takes a positive tag. You are coming, aren't you? and You aren't coming, are you? are both correct. The tag never repeats the polarity of the statement. A sentence such as She is a doctor, is she? is wrong because both halves are positive; the correct tag is isn't she?

The tense and the auxiliary must match the statement exactly. If the statement uses is, the tag uses isn't; if it uses has, the tag uses hasn't; if it uses will, the tag uses won't. If the statement uses a simple present with no auxiliary, the tag uses don't or doesn't; if it uses a simple past with no auxiliary, the tag uses didn't. The main verb is not repeated in the tag: She likes tea, doesn't she? and not She likes tea, doesn't like she?

The pronoun in the tag must be a subject pronoun, not a name and not an object pronoun. Rina is coming, isn't she? is correct; Rina is coming, isn't Rina? is wrong. A noun subject is replaced by he, she, it or they according to number and gender. Two subjects joined by and take they: Rina and Mina are coming, aren't they? A singular subject with each or every also takes they in informal use, though the singular is preferred in careful writing.

Several special subjects have fixed tags. The subject I am takes aren't I in standard spoken English, not amn't I. The subject let's takes shall we: Let's go, shall we? An imperative takes will you, would you, can you or could you: Close the door, will you? A sentence beginning with nothing, nobody, no one, none or neither takes a positive tag with it or they: Nothing happened, did it? Nobody came, did they?

Words that make a sentence negative without a visible not also change the tag. Never, hardly, scarcely, barely, seldom, rarely, no longer and little are negative in meaning, so the tag is positive. She never comes late, does she? and He hardly speaks, does he? are correct. A sentence with a negative prefix such as unhappy or impossible is still grammatically positive, so it takes a negative tag: She is unhappy, isn't she?

The tag is separated by a comma in writing, and the pronoun and auxiliary are contracted in speech and usually in writing. The intonation decides the meaning: a falling tone expects agreement, and a rising tone asks a real question. In the examination only the written form matters, so the safe habit is to check four things in order: the auxiliary, the polarity, the pronoun and the tense.

A modal is a helping verb that adds meaning such as ability, permission, obligation, advice, possibility or deduction. The main modals are can, could, may, might, must, shall, should, will and would, and the semi-modals are ought to, need, dare, used to and had better. A modal is followed by the base form of the main verb, without to, except for ought to, used to and had better. There is no s on a modal: he can, not he cans; she must, not she musts.

Questions and negatives with modals are made without do. We say Can he swim? and not Does he can swim? and He cannot swim, not He does not can swim. The negative of can is cannot, written as one word, or can't in speech. The negative of must is must not or mustn't for prohibition, while need not or don't have to expresses absence of obligation. The difference between mustn't and needn't is a favourite question: you mustn't smoke means smoking is forbidden, and you needn't smoke means smoking is not necessary.

Ability is expressed by can in the present and could in the past: She can drive; She could drive when she was eighteen. Permission is expressed by can, may or could, with may the most formal: May I come in? Possibility is expressed by may, might or could: It may rain; It might rain; It could rain. Deduction about the present is expressed by must: The light is on, so he must be at home. Deduction about the past is expressed by must have with the past participle: He must have forgotten.

Obligation and advice are expressed by must, should, ought to and had better. Must is strong and often comes from the speaker; have to is used for external obligation. Should and ought to give advice and are followed by the base form and to respectively. Had better carries a warning and takes the base form without to: You had better see a doctor. The negative had better not is used for advice against an action.

The modal perfect is a common exam point. Modal plus have plus past participle looks back at a past action. Should have done means the action was right but was not done, and it carries regret or criticism. Could have done means the action was possible but was not done. Might have done means it was possible. Must have done means the speaker is almost certain. Needn't have done means the action was done but was unnecessary, which is different from needn't do, where the action was not done at all.
A positive statement takes a negative tag; a negative statement takes a positive tag.
The tag repeats the auxiliary and the tense of the statement, and uses a subject pronoun.
If there is no auxiliary, the tag uses do, does or did.
I am takes aren't I; let's takes shall we; imperatives take will you.
Never, hardly, seldom and no longer make the statement negative, so the tag is positive.
A modal is followed by the base verb and never takes s or do-support.
Mustn't is prohibition; needn't is absence of obligation.
Modal plus have plus past participle refers to the past.

She has finished her work, hasn't she? The statement uses the auxiliary has, so the tag repeats hasn't, and the subject is replaced by she. The polarity is positive to negative, which is correct. If the statement were She hasn't finished her work, the tag would be has she?

Nobody phoned, did they? Nobody is negative in meaning, so the tag must be positive. The pronoun for nobody is they in modern usage, and the auxiliary for the past simple is did. The tag is therefore did they?

You needn't have waited for me. The sentence means that waiting was unnecessary, but it happened. If the person had not waited, the correct sentence would be You needn't wait for me. The difference between needn't have waited and needn't wait is exactly what the modal-perfect question tests.

He must have missed the train. Must have plus the past participle expresses a strong deduction about the past. If the sentence were about the present, it would be He must be late, without have. The past participle missed is required after have.
Repeating the same polarity in both halves.
Using a name instead of a pronoun in the tag.
Forgetting do-support when the statement has no auxiliary.
Using amn't I instead of aren't I.
Treating never or hardly as positive and giving a negative tag.
Adding s to a modal or using do with a modal.
Using the base verb instead of the past participle after modal plus have.

For a question tag, check the auxiliary, the polarity, the pronoun and the tense in that order. For a modal, check that the next verb is in the base form and that no do or s has crept in. Both checks take a few seconds and save easy marks.
as: প্ৰশ্ন টেগ (question tag) হৈছে বাক্যৰ শেষত যোগ কৰা চুটি প্ৰশ্ন, যেনে You are coming, aren't you? টেগে বাক্যটো নিশ্চিত কৰাৰ অনুৰোধলৈ সলনি কৰে, আৰু ই পত্ৰৰ আটাইতকৈ সহজতে নম্বৰ হেৰুওৱা ঠাইবোৰৰ এটা, কাৰণ নিয়মটোৰ কেইবাটাও সৰু অংশ আছে। টেগ দুটা অংশৰ পৰা গঠিত: বাক্যৰ সহায়ক ক্ৰিয়া আৰু কৰ্তাক প্ৰতিনিধিত্ব কৰা সৰ্বনাম। বাক্যত সহায়ক ক্ৰিয়া নাথাকিলে টেগে do, does বা did লয়, আৰু মূল ক্ৰিয়া base form লৈ ঘূৰি যায়।

পোলাৰিটি নিয়মটো প্ৰথমে প্ৰয়োগ কৰিব লাগে। ধনাত্মক বাক্যই ঋণাত্মক টেগ লয়, আৰু ঋণাত্মক বাক্যই ধনাত্মক টেগ লয়। You are coming, aren't you? আৰু You aren't coming, are you? দুয়োটা শুদ্ধ। টেগে বাক্যৰ পোলাৰিটি পুনৰাবৃত্তি নকৰে। She is a doctor, is she? ভুল, কাৰণ দুয়ো অৰ্ধ ধনাত্মক; শুদ্ধ টেগ isn't she?

কাল আৰু সহায়ক ক্ৰিয়া বাক্যৰ সৈতে হুবহু মিলিব লাগে। বাক্যই is ল'লে টেগে isn't লয়; has ল'লে hasn't; will ল'লে won't। বাক্যই সহায়ক নোহোৱা simple present ল'লে টেগে don't বা doesn't লয়; simple past ল'লে didn't। টেগত মূল ক্ৰিয়া পুনৰাবৃত্তি নহয়: She likes tea, doesn't she? শুদ্ধ, She likes tea, doesn't like she? ভুল।

টেগৰ সৰ্বনাম subject pronoun হ'ব লাগে, নাম বা object pronoun নহয়। Rina is coming, isn't she? শুদ্ধ; Rina is coming, isn't Rina? ভুল। বিশেষ্য কৰ্তাক সংখ্যা আৰু লিংগ অনুসৰি he, she, it বা they ৰে সলোৱা হয়। and ৰে জোড়া দুটা কৰ্তাই they লয়: Rina and Mina are coming, aren't they? each বা every থকা একবচন কৰ্তাও অনানুষ্ঠানিক ব্যৱহাৰত they লয়, যদিও যতনশীল লিখাত একবচন শ্ৰেয়।

কিছুমান বিশেষ কৰ্তাৰ নিৰ্দিষ্ট টেগ আছে। কৰ্তা I am ৰ টেগ মানক কথিত ইংৰাজীত aren't I, amn't I নহয়। কৰ্তা let's ৰ টেগ shall we: Let's go, shall we? Imperative ৰ টেগ will you, would you, can you বা could you: Close the door, will you? nothing, nobody, no one, none বা neither ৰে আৰম্ভ হোৱা বাক্যই it বা they ৰে ধনাত্মক টেগ লয়: Nothing happened, did it? Nobody came, did they?

দেখাকৈ not নোহোৱাকৈ বাক্যক ঋণাত্মক কৰা শব্দবোৰেও টেগ সলায়। Never, hardly, scarcely, barely, seldom, rarely, no longer আৰু little অৰ্থত ঋণাত্মক, গতিকে টেগ ধনাত্মক। She never comes late, does she? আৰু He hardly speaks, does he? শুদ্ধ। unhappy বা impossible যেনে ঋণাত্মক উপসৰ্গ থকা বাক্য ব্যাকৰণত ধনাত্মক, গতিকে ঋণাত্মক টেগ লয়: She is unhappy, isn't she?

লিখাত টেগ কমাৰে পৃথক কৰা হয়, আৰু কথনত তথা সাধাৰণতে লিখাত সৰ্বনাম আৰু সহায়ক ক্ৰিয়া সংক্ষিপ্ত কৰা হয়। স্বৰে অৰ্থ নিৰ্ণয় কৰে: নমা স্বৰে সহমত আশা কৰে, উঠা স্বৰে প্ৰকৃত প্ৰশ্ন সোধে। পৰীক্ষাত কেৱল লিখিত ৰূপটোৱেই গুৰুত্বপূৰ্ণ, গতিকে নিৰাপদ অভ্যাস হৈছে এই চাৰিটা ক্ৰমে পৰীক্ষা কৰা: সহায়ক ক্ৰিয়া, পোলাৰিটি, সৰ্বনাম আৰু কাল।

Modal হৈছে সহায়ক ক্ৰিয়া যিয়ে সামৰ্থ্য, অনুমতি, বাধ্যবাধকতা, পৰামৰ্শ, সম্ভাৱনা বা অনুমানৰ অৰ্থ যোগ কৰে। মূল modal হৈছে can, could, may, might, must, shall, should, will আৰু would, আৰু semi-modal হৈছে ought to, need, dare, used to আৰু had better। Modal ৰ পিছত মূল ক্ৰিয়াৰ base form আহে, to ৰ বাহিৰে, ought to, used to আৰু had better ৰ ক্ষেত্ৰত। Modal ত s নাই: he can, he cans নহয়; she must, she musts নহয়।

Modal ৰ প্ৰশ্ন আৰু ঋণাত্মক ৰূপ do ৰ অবিহনে গঠিত হয়। আমি Can he swim? লিখোঁ, Does he can swim? নহয়, আৰু He cannot swim, He does not can swim নহয়। can ৰ ঋণাত্মক cannot, এটা শব্দ হিচাপে, বা কথনত can't। must ৰ ঋণাত্মক must not বা mustn't নিষেধৰ বাবে, আনহাতে need not বা don't have to বাধ্যবাধকতাৰ অনুপস্থিতি বুজায়। mustn't আৰু needn't ৰ পাৰ্থক্য প্ৰিয় প্ৰশ্ন: you mustn't smoke মানে ধূমপান নিষিদ্ধ, you needn't smoke মানে ধূমপান আৱশ্যক নহয়।

সামৰ্থ্য বৰ্তমানত can আৰু অতীতত could ৰে বুজোৱা হয়: তাই গাড়ী চলাব পাৰে; তাই ওঠৰ বছৰত গাড়ী চলাব পাৰিছিল। অনুমতি can, may বা could ৰে, may আটাইতকৈ আনুষ্ঠানিক: May I come in? সম্ভাৱনা may, might বা could ৰে: বৰষুণ দিব পাৰে। বৰ্তমানৰ অনুমান must ৰে: পোহৰ জ্বলি আছে, গতিকে তেওঁ ঘৰত থাকিবই। অতীতৰ অনুমান must have ৰ লগত past participle ৰে: তেওঁ পাহৰি থাকিবই।

বাধ্যবাধকতা আৰু পৰামৰ্শ must, should, ought to আৰু had better ৰে বুজোৱা হয়। Must শক্তিশালী আৰু প্ৰায়ে বক্তাৰ পৰা আহে; have to বাহ্যিক বাধ্যবাধকতাৰ বাবে। Should আৰু ought to পৰামৰ্শ দিয়ে আৰু ক্ৰমে base form আৰু to লয়। Had better সতৰ্কবাণী বহন কৰে আৰু to ৰ অবিহনে base form লয়: You had better see a doctor। বিৰোধী কামৰ পৰামৰ্শৰ বাবে had better not ব্যৱহাৰ হয়।

Modal perfect এটা সাধাৰণ পৰীক্ষা বিন্দু। Modal + have + past participle এ অতীতৰ কামলৈ ঘূৰি চায়। Should have done মানে কামটো কৰা উচিত আছিল কিন্তু কৰা নহ'ল, আৰু ই অনুশোচনা বা সমালোচনা বহন কৰে। Could have done মানে কামটো সম্ভৱ আছিল কিন্তু কৰা নহ'ল। Might have done মানে সম্ভৱ আছিল। Must have done মানে বক্তা প্ৰায় নিশ্চিত। Needn't have done মানে কামটো হৈছে কিন্তু আৱশ্যক নাছিল, যি needn't do ৰ পৰা বেলেগ, য'ত কামটো একেবাৰে হোৱা নাই।

কিছুমান অৰ্ধ-সহায়ক ক্ৰিয়াৰ টেগত সাৱধানতা লাগে। used to ৰ টেগ didn't: He used to smoke, didn't he? had better ৰ টেগ hadn't: You had better go, hadn't you? would rather ৰ টেগ wouldn't: You would rather stay, wouldn't you? ought to ৰ টেগ shouldn't বা oughtn't: She ought to apologise, shouldn't she? এইবোৰত বাক্যৰ সহায়ক ক্ৰিয়াৰ পৰিৱৰ্তে সেই অৰ্ধ-সহায়ক ক্ৰিয়াৰ সৈতে জড়িত ৰূপটো ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা হয়, আৰু প্ৰশ্নই প্ৰায়ে এই ৰূপবোৰৰ এটা সোধে।

Modal ৰ তুলনাও প্ৰায়ে সোধা হয়। Can সামৰ্থ্যৰ বাবে, be able to ৰূপ বা কালৰ প্ৰয়োজনত can ৰ ঠাইত: She will be able to come, She will can come নহয়। Must ভিতৰৰ বাধ্যবাধকতাৰ বাবে, have to বাহিৰৰ বাধ্যবাধকতাৰ বাবে, আৰু অতীতত must ৰ সলনি had to: Yesterday I had to work late, Yesterday I must work late নহয়। Would অতীতৰ অভ্যাসৰ বাবে, used to ৰ সৈতে, কিন্তু would কেৱল ক্ৰিয়াৰ বাবে: We would visit our grandmother every summer। This house used to be a school, This house would be a school নহয়, কাৰণ অৱস্থা এটাৰ বাবে used to লাগে।
ধনাত্মক বাক্যই ঋণাত্মক টেগ, ঋণাত্মক বাক্যই ধনাত্মক টেগ লয়।
টেগে বাক্যৰ সহায়ক ক্ৰিয়া আৰু কাল পুনৰাবৃত্তি কৰে, আৰু subject pronoun লয়।
সহায়ক ক্ৰিয়া নাথাকিলে টেগে do, does বা did লয়।
I am ৰ টেগ aren't I; let's ৰ shall we; imperative ৰ will you।
never, hardly, seldom, no longer এ বাক্যক ঋণাত্মক কৰে, গতিকে টেগ ধনাত্মক।
Modal ৰ পিছত base verb, আৰু modal ত s বা do-support নাই।
Modal + have + past participle এ অতীতলৈ নিৰ্দেশ কৰে।

She has finished her work, hasn't she? বাক্যই সহায়ক has লৈছে, গতিকে টেগে hasn't পুনৰাবৃত্তি কৰে, আৰু কৰ্তাক she ৰে সলোৱা হয়। পোলাৰিটি ধনাত্মকৰ পৰা ঋণাত্মক, যি শুদ্ধ। যদি বাক্য She hasn't finished her work হ'লহেঁতেন, টেগ has she? হ'লহেঁতেন।
Nobody phoned, did they? Nobody অৰ্থত ঋণাত্মক, গতিকে টেগ ধনাত্মক হ'ব লাগে। আধুনিক ব্যৱহাৰত nobody ৰ সৰ্বনাম they, আৰু past simple ৰ সহায়ক did। গতিকে টেগ did they?

You needn't have waited for me। বাক্যটোৰ অৰ্থ অপেক্ষা আৱশ্যক নাছিল, কিন্তু হৈছে। যদি ব্যক্তিজনে অপেক্ষা নকৰিলেহেঁতেন, শুদ্ধ বাক্য You needn't wait for me হ'লহেঁতেন। needn't have waited আৰু needn't wait ৰ পাৰ্থক্যটোৱেই modal-perfect প্ৰশ্নই পৰীক্ষা কৰে।

He must have missed the train। Must have ৰ লগত past participle এ অতীতৰ বিষয়ে দৃঢ় অনুমান বুজায়। যদি বাক্যটো বৰ্তমানৰ বিষয়ে হ'লহেঁতেন, তেন্তে He must be late, have ৰ অবিহনে। have ৰ পিছত past participle missed আৱশ্যক।
দুয়ো অৰ্ধত একেই পোলাৰিটি পুনৰাবৃত্তি কৰা।
টেগত নাম ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা, সৰ্বনামৰ সলনি।
সহায়ক ক্ৰিয়া নাথাকিলে do-support পাহৰি যোৱা।
amn't I ৰ সলনি aren't I ব্যৱহাৰ নকৰা।
never বা hardly ক ধনাত্মক ধৰি ঋণাত্মক টেগ দিয়া।
modal ত s যোগ কৰা বা modal ৰ লগত do ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা।
mustn't আৰু needn't ৰ মাজত বিভ্ৰান্ত হোৱা।
modal + have ৰ পিছত base verb ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা, past participle ৰ সলনি।

প্ৰশ্ন টেগৰ বাবে সহায়ক ক্ৰিয়া, পোলাৰিটি, সৰ্বনাম আৰু কাল এই ক্ৰমে পৰীক্ষা কৰক। Modal ৰ বাবে পৰৱৰ্তী ক্ৰিয়া base form নেকি আৰু do বা s সোমাই পৰা নাই নেকি চাওক। দুয়ো পৰীক্ষাই কেইছেকেণ্ড লয় আৰু সহজ নম্বৰ ৰক্ষা কৰে।

en: A conjunction is a word that joins two words, two phrases or two clauses. It is the hinge of the sentence: without it the two parts either stand apart or collide. In the DHS and DME Technical Grade III paper the conjunction is not asked as a definition but as a choice between four linkers, and the choice depends on the relation between the two ideas. The candidate has to decide whether the second idea adds, contrasts, gives a reason, gives a result, states a condition or states a concession, and then pick the linker that carries that relation.

There are three families. Coordinating conjunctions join two parts of equal grammatical rank, and the common ones are remembered by the group for, and, nor, but, or, yet and so. Subordinating conjunctions join a dependent clause to a main clause, and they carry the meaning of time, cause, condition, concession, purpose or result. Correlative conjunctions work in pairs, such as either ... or, neither ... nor, both ... and, not only ... but also, and no sooner ... than. A fourth group, the conjunctive adverbs such as however, therefore, moreover and nevertheless, looks like a conjunction but behaves like an adverb and needs a semicolon or a full stop before it.

The coordinating conjunctions are the easiest to master because there are only seven. And adds; but contrasts; or offers an alternative; nor adds a second negative; for gives a reason in a formal style; yet contrasts with a sense of surprise; so gives a result. A useful memory aid is the word FANBOYS, formed from the first letters of for, and, nor, but, or, yet and so. Each of these can join two words, two phrases or two independent clauses, and when it joins two independent clauses a comma usually comes before it.

The subordinating conjunctions are larger in number and are grouped by meaning. Time: when, while, before, after, until, till, since, as soon as, whenever. Cause: because, since, as, now that. Condition: if, unless, provided that, in case, on condition that. Concession: although, though, even though, whereas, while. Purpose: so that, in order that, lest. Result: so ... that, such ... that. Comparison: than, as ... as. A candidate who can name the group of a linker can reject the options that belong to another group without reading the whole sentence.

Correlative conjunctions must be balanced. Either goes with or, neither with nor, both with and, not only with but also, and no sooner with than. The parts joined must be parallel: either the book or the pen, not either the book or pen. When not only comes at the beginning of a sentence for emphasis, the subject and auxiliary are inverted: Not only did he sing, but he also danced. When neither ... nor joins two subjects, the verb agrees with the nearer subject: Neither the teacher nor the students were present.

Two fixed patterns cause most of the errors. No sooner is followed by than, and the clause after no sooner takes the past perfect with inversion: No sooner had he arrived than it began to rain. Hardly and scarcely are followed by when: Hardly had he arrived when it began to rain. The word than never follows hardly or scarcely, and when never follows no sooner. These three patterns are asked so often that they are worth writing on a card.

A second fixed pattern is the pair though ... yet and although ... yet. In careful English we do not use though with but: Although he was tired, but he continued is wrong. The correct forms are Although he was tired, he continued, or He was tired, but he continued. The same applies to because and so: Because it rained, so the match was cancelled is wrong; use either Because it rained, the match was cancelled, or It rained, so the match was cancelled.

Lest is a formal conjunction that already carries a negative sense, so it is followed by should and never by not: Work hard lest you should fail. The phrase for fear that works in the same way. Unless already means if not, so unless you do not go is a double negative; the correct form is unless you go. Since can mean because or from the time that, and the context decides which; a sentence such as Since he left, we have heard nothing uses the time sense, while Since he is ill, he will not come uses the cause sense.

Conjunctive adverbs are often mistaken for conjunctions. However, therefore, moreover, nevertheless, consequently and otherwise join two independent clauses, but they do not join them grammatically; they need a semicolon or a full stop before them, and a comma after them. He was tired; however, he continued is correct. He was tired, however he continued is wrong because a comma alone cannot join two independent clauses. This is a favourite of the punctuation-and-correction question.

The conjunction must also match the logic of the sentence. A cause needs because or since, not but. A contrast needs but, yet, although or whereas, not so. A result needs so or therefore, not because. A condition needs if or unless, not although. In the examination the four options often belong to four different groups, and the logic of the two clauses alone is enough to reject three of them. Reading the relation first, and the linker second, is the fastest safe method.
Coordinating conjunctions join equals: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so.
Subordinating conjunctions join a dependent clause to a main clause and carry time, cause, condition, concession, purpose or result.
Correlative pairs must be balanced: either ... or, neither ... nor, both ... and, not only ... but also, no sooner ... than.
No sooner takes than; hardly and scarcely take when.
Do not use though with but, or because with so.
Conjunctive adverbs need a semicolon or full stop before them.
Match the linker to the relation between the clauses.

He was ill, ___ he attended the class. The relation is contrast, so the linker is but or yet. Because would give a reason, so would give a result, and and would add, none of which fits the surprise of attending while ill.

___ he had finished his work, he went home. The relation is time, and the action in the first clause is complete before the second, so after is correct. Before would reverse the order, while would overlap the two actions, and unless would make the first clause a condition.

No sooner ___ the bell rang than the students left. The correct form is had the bell rung, because no sooner takes the past perfect with inversion. The word than is already in the sentence and must not be replaced by when. The full sentence is No sooner had the bell rung than the students left.

She is not only a good singer ___ a good dancer. The pair is not only ... but also, so the blank takes but also. The word and alone would break the pair, and or would change the meaning. The two qualities are both true, so the additive pair is required.
Using though with but, or because with so.
Writing no sooner ... when, or hardly ... than.
Breaking a correlative pair, as in not only ... and.
Joining two independent clauses with only a comma and however.
Choosing a linker from the wrong meaning group.

Before you look at the options, name the relation between the two clauses in one word: addition, contrast, reason, result, condition, concession, time or purpose. Then choose the linker from that group. The relation is in the sentence; the linker is only its label.
as: সংযোগ (conjunction) হৈছে দুটা শব্দ, দুটা বাক্যাংশ বা দুটা উপবাক্য জোড়া শব্দ। ই বাক্যৰ কব্জা: ইয়াৰ অবিহনে দুয়ো অংশ হয় পৃথক হৈ থাকে, নহয় সংঘৰ্ষ কৰে। DHS আৰু DME কাৰিকৰী গ্ৰেড III পত্ৰত সংযোগ সংজ্ঞা হিচাপে নহয়, চাৰিটা linker ৰ মাজৰ বাছনি হিচাপে আহে, আৰু বাছনিটো দুয়ো ভাৱৰ সম্পৰ্কৰ ওপৰত নিৰ্ভৰ কৰে। প্ৰাৰ্থীয়ে নিৰ্ণয় কৰিব লাগে দ্বিতীয় ভাৱটো যোগ কৰে, বিৰোধ কৰে, কাৰণ দিয়ে, ফল দিয়ে, চৰ্ত দিয়ে নে ছাৰ দিয়ে, আৰু তাৰ পিছত সেই সম্পৰ্ক বহন কৰা linker বাছিব লাগে।

তিনিটা পৰিয়াল আছে। সমপদীয় সংযোগে সমান ব্যাকৰণিক স্থানৰ দুটা অংশ জোড়ে, আৰু সাধাৰণবোৰ for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so গোটেৰে মনত ৰখা হয়। অধীনতাবাচক সংযোগে এটা আশ্ৰিত উপবাক্যক মূল উপবাক্যৰ লগত জোড়ে, আৰু সিহঁতে সময়, কাৰণ, চৰ্ত, ছাৰ, উদ্দেশ্য বা ফলৰ অৰ্থ বহন কৰে। যুগল সংযোগ যোৰ হিচাপে চলে, যেনে either ... or, neither ... nor, both ... and, not only ... but also, no sooner ... than। চতুৰ্থ গোট, conjunctive adverb যেনে however, therefore, moreover, nevertheless, সংযোগ যেন দেখায় কিন্তু ক্ৰিয়া-বিশেষণৰ দৰে চলে আৰু তাৰ আগত semicolon বা পূৰ্ণবিৰাম লাগে।

সমপদীয় সংযোগ সাতটাই, গতিকে আয়ত্ত কৰা সহজ। And যোগ কৰে; but বিৰোধ কৰে; or বিকল্প দিয়ে; nor দ্বিতীয় ঋণাত্মক যোগ কৰে; for আনুষ্ঠানিক ৰীতিত কাৰণ দিয়ে; yet আচৰিত ভাৱে বিৰোধ কৰে; so ফল দিয়ে। FANBOYS শব্দটো মনত ৰখাৰ সহায়, যি for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so ৰ প্ৰথম আখৰেৰে গঠিত। ইহঁতৰ প্ৰতিটোৱে দুটা শব্দ, দুটা বাক্যাংশ বা দুটা স্বাধীন উপবাক্য জোড়ে, আৰু দুটা স্বাধীন উপবাক্য জোড়িলে সাধাৰণতে তাৰ আগত কমা আহে।

অধীনতাবাচক সংযোগ সংখ্যাত বেছি আৰু অৰ্থ অনুসৰি গোটত বিভক্ত। সময়: when, while, before, after, until, till, since, as soon as, whenever। কাৰণ: because, since, as, now that। চৰ্ত: if, unless, provided that, in case, on condition that। ছাৰ: although, though, even though, whereas, while। উদ্দেশ্য: so that, in order that, lest। ফল: so ... that, such ... that। তুলনা: than, as ... as। যি প্ৰাৰ্থীয়ে linker ৰ গোট ক'ব জানে, তেওঁ গোটেই বাক্য নপঢ়াকৈ আন গোটৰ বিকল্প নাকচ কৰিব পাৰে।

যুগল সংযোগ ভাৰসাম্যত থাকিব লাগে। Either ৰ লগত or, neither ৰ লগত nor, both ৰ লগত and, not only ৰ লগত but also, আৰু no sooner ৰ লগত than। জোড়া অংশ সমান্তৰাল হ'ব লাগে: either the book or the pen, either the book or pen নহয়। জোৰ দিবলৈ not only বাক্যৰ আৰম্ভণিত থাকিলে কৰ্তা আৰু সহায়ক ক্ৰিয়া ওলোটা হয়: Not only did he sing, but he also danced। যেতিয়া neither ... nor এ দুটা কৰ্তা জোড়ে, ক্ৰিয়া নিকটৱৰ্তী কৰ্তাৰ সৈতে মিলে: Neither the teacher nor the students were present।

দুটা নিৰ্দিষ্ট আৰ্হিয়ে বেছিভাগ ভুল কৰে। No sooner ৰ পিছত than আহে, আৰু no sooner ৰ পিছৰ উপবাক্যই ওলোটা সহিত past perfect লয়: No sooner had he arrived than it began to rain। Hardly আৰু scarcely ৰ পিছত when আহে: Hardly had he arrived when it began to rain। hardly বা scarcely ৰ পিছত than কেতিয়াও নাহে, আৰু no sooner ৰ পিছত when কেতিয়াও নাহে। এই তিনিটা আৰ্হি ইমানেই সোধা হয় যে কাৰ্ডত লিখি ৰখাৰ যোগ্য।

দ্বিতীয় নিৰ্দিষ্ট আৰ্হি হৈছে though ... yet আৰু although ... yet ৰ যোৰ। যতনশীল ইংৰাজীত though ৰ লগত but ব্যৱহাৰ নকৰোঁ: Although he was tired, but he continued ভুল। শুদ্ধ ৰূপ Although he was tired, he continued, বা He was tired, but he continued। একেই কথা because আৰু so ৰ বাবেও: Because it rained, so the match was cancelled ভুল; Because it rained, the match was cancelled, বা It rained, so the match was cancelled ব্যৱহাৰ কৰক।

Lest এটা আনুষ্ঠানিক সংযোগ যিয়ে ইতিমধ্যে ঋণাত্মক ভাৱ বহন কৰে, গতিকে তাৰ পিছত should আহে, not কেতিয়াও নাহে: Work hard lest you should fail। for fear that বাক্যাংশও একেই ধৰণে চলে। Unless ৰ অৰ্থ ইতিমধ্যে if not, গতিকে unless you do not go দ্বৈত ঋণাত্মক; শুদ্ধ ৰূপ unless you go। Since ৰ অৰ্থ because বা from the time that হ'ব পাৰে, আৰু প্ৰসংগে নিৰ্ণয় কৰে; Since he left, we have heard nothing ত সময়ৰ অৰ্থ, আনহাতে Since he is ill, he will not come ত কাৰণৰ অৰ্থ।

Conjunctive adverb ক প্ৰায়ে সংযোগ বুলি ভুল কৰা হয়। However, therefore, moreover, nevertheless, consequently, otherwise এ দুটা স্বাধীন উপবাক্য জোড়ে, কিন্তু ব্যাকৰণিকভাৱে জোড়া নিদিয়ে; তাৰ আগত semicolon বা পূৰ্ণবিৰাম লাগে, আৰু পিছত কমা লাগে। He was tired; however, he continued শুদ্ধ। He was tired, however he continued ভুল, কাৰণ কেৱল কমাৰে দুটা স্বাধীন উপবাক্য জোড়া নিদিয়ে। এইটো যতি-চিহ্ন আৰু শুধৰণিৰ প্ৰশ্নৰ প্ৰিয়।

সংযোগে বাক্যৰ যুক্তিৰ সৈতেও মিলিব লাগে। কাৰণৰ বাবে because বা since, but নহয়। বিৰোধৰ বাবে but, yet, although বা whereas, so নহয়। ফলৰ বাবে so বা therefore, because নহয়। চৰ্তৰ বাবে if বা unless, although নহয়। পৰীক্ষাত চাৰিটা বিকল্প প্ৰায়ে চাৰিটা বেলেগ গোটৰ হয়, আৰু দুয়ো উপবাক্যৰ যুক্তিয়েই তিনিটা নাকচ কৰিবলৈ যথেষ্ট। প্ৰথমে সম্পৰ্ক আৰু দ্বিতীয়তে linker পঢ়াই আটাইতকৈ দ্ৰুত নিৰাপদ পদ্ধতি।

একে শব্দই সংযোগ আৰু পূৰ্বসৰ্গ দুয়োটা হ'ব পাৰে, আৰু পৰীক্ষাই এই পাৰ্থক্যটো সোধে। Before, after, since, till, until আৰু as ৰ পিছত উপবাক্য থাকিলে সেয়া সংযোগ, কিন্তু বিশেষ্য বা বাক্যাংশ থাকিলে পূৰ্বসৰ্গ: He left before the bell rang (সংযোগ), He left before the bell (পূৰ্বসৰ্গ)। But সাধাৰণতে সংযোগ, কিন্তু no one but him ত সেয়া পূৰ্বসৰ্গৰ দৰে কাম কৰে। গতিকে শব্দটো নহয়, তাৰ পিছত কি আহিছে সেয়াই ভূমিকা নিৰ্ণয় কৰে।

তুলনাৰ যোৰতো সাৱধানতা লাগে। সমতাৰ বাবে as ... as, অসমতাৰ বাবে not so ... as: She is as tall as her sister, She is not so tall as her sister। so ... that আৰু such ... that ৰ পাৰ্থক্য মন কৰক: so বিশেষণ বা ক্ৰিয়া-বিশেষণৰ লগত, such বিশেষ্যৰ লগত: He was so tired that he slept, It was such a tiring day that he slept। such a ৰ ক্ৰম such + a + বিশেষণ + বিশেষ্য, আৰু so ৰ ক্ৰম so + বিশেষণ + a + বিশেষ্য: so tiring a day। এই ক্ৰমবোৰ ভুল কৰাটো সাধাৰণ, আৰু প্ৰতিটোৱেই এটা নম্বৰ।
সমপদীয় সংযোগে সমান জোড়ে: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so।
অধীনতাবাচক সংযোগে আশ্ৰিত উপবাক্যক মূল উপবাক্যৰ লগত জোড়ে আৰু সময়, কাৰণ, চৰ্ত, ছাৰ, উদ্দেশ্য বা ফল বহন কৰে।
যুগল যোৰ ভাৰসাম্যত থাকিব: either ... or, neither ... nor, both ... and, not only ... but also, no sooner ... than।
No sooner ৰ লগত than; hardly আৰু scarcely ৰ লগত when।
though ৰ লগত but, বা because ৰ লগত so নিদিব।
Lest ৰ লগত should, not নহয়।
Conjunctive adverb ৰ আগত semicolon বা পূৰ্ণবিৰাম লাগে।
He was ill, ___ he attended the class। সম্পৰ্ক বিৰোধ, গতিকে linker but বা yet। Because এ কাৰণ দিব, so এ ফল দিব, and এ যোগ কৰিব, কিন্তু অসুস্থ হৈও শ্ৰেণীত উপস্থিত থকাৰ আচৰিত ভাৱত এটাও খাপ নাখায়।

___ he had finished his work, he went home। সম্পৰ্ক সময়, আৰু প্ৰথম উপবাক্যৰ কাম দ্বিতীয়ৰ আগতে সম্পূৰ্ণ, গতিকে after শুদ্ধ। Before এ ক্ৰম ওলোটা কৰিব, while এ দুয়ো কাম একেলগে দেখুৱাব, আৰু unless এ প্ৰথম উপবাক্যক চৰ্ত কৰিব।

No sooner ___ the bell rang than the students left। শুদ্ধ ৰূপ had the bell rung, কাৰণ no sooner ৰ লগত ওলোটা সহিত past perfect আহে। than ইতিমধ্যে বাক্যত আছে আৰু when ৰে সলাব নালাগে। সম্পূৰ্ণ বাক্য No sooner had the bell rung than the students left।
She is not only a good singer ___ a good dancer। যোৰ not only ... but also, গতিকে ৰিক্ত স্থানত but also। কেৱল and এ যোৰ ভাঙিব, or এ অৰ্থ সলাব। দুয়ো গুণ সত্য, গতিকে যোগাত্মক যোৰ আৱশ্যক।
though ৰ লগত but, বা because ৰ লগত so ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা।
no sooner ... when, বা hardly ... than লিখা।
যুগল যোৰ ভঙা, যেনে not only ... and।
unless ৰ লগত আন ঋণাত্মক ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা।
দুটা স্বাধীন উপবাক্য কেৱল কমা আৰু however ৰে জোড়া।

বিকল্প চোৱাৰ আগতে দুয়ো উপবাক্যৰ সম্পৰ্ক এটা শব্দত কওক: যোগ, বিৰোধ, কাৰণ, ফল, চৰ্ত, ছাৰ, সময় বা উদ্দেশ্য। তাৰ পিছত সেই গোটৰ পৰা linker বাছক। সম্পৰ্ক বাক্যত থাকে; linker মাত্ৰ তাৰ লেবেল। এই এটা অভ্যাসে চাৰিটা বিকল্পৰ পৰা তিনিটা লগে লগে আঁতৰাই দিয়ে আৰু সময় বচায়।

en: A finite verb changes with the subject and the tense: I go, she goes, they went. A non-finite verb does not change in that way, and it cannot be the only verb of a sentence. English has three non-finite forms: the infinitive, which is to plus the base verb, as in to write; the gerund, which is the ing form used as a noun, as in writing; and the participle, which is either the present participle writing or the past participle written. The DHS and DME Technical Grade III paper tests these forms through verb patterns, error spotting and sentence correction, not through definitions.

The infinitive has several jobs. It can be the subject of a sentence, though this is formal: To err is human. It can be the object of a verb: She wants to sing. It can express purpose: He went to the market to buy rice. It can follow an adjective: I am glad to meet you. It can follow a noun: He has the ability to solve it. And it can be the complement of be: My aim is to serve. The bare infinitive, without to, follows modals, let, make, see, hear, feel and watch: She can swim; Let him go; I saw him leave.

The gerund is the ing form doing the work of a noun. It can be the subject: Swimming is good exercise. It can be the object: She enjoys reading. It can follow a preposition: He is good at painting; She insisted on coming. It can follow certain verbs: avoid, enjoy, mind, finish, suggest, recommend, consider, admit, deny, postpone, practise, risk, keep and look forward to. After a preposition, the verb must be a gerund, never an infinitive: She is interested in learning, not interested in to learn.

Some verbs take either form but with a change of meaning. Stop doing means to end an action; stop to do means to pause in order to do something else. Remember doing means to recall a past action; remember to do means not to forget a future duty. Forget doing means to lose the memory of a past action; forget to do means to fail to do a duty. Regret doing means to be sorry about the past; regret to do is used for announcing bad news. Try doing means to experiment; try to do means to make an effort. Go on doing means to continue; go on to do means to move to the next item. Mean doing means to involve as a result; mean to do means to intend.

The present participle has two main uses. It forms the continuous tenses with be: She is writing. It also works as an adjective: a running tap, a crying child, an interesting book. The past participle forms the perfect tenses with have and the passive with be: She has written; The letter was written. It also works as an adjective: a broken window, a written test, a tired traveller. The difference between an interesting book and an interested reader is the difference between the present participle, which causes the feeling, and the past participle, which receives it.

The dangling participle is a common error. A participle at the beginning of a sentence must describe the subject of the main clause. Walking down the road, I saw a snake is correct, because I was walking. Walking down the road, a snake was seen is wrong, because the snake was not walking. The same rule applies to the perfect participle: Having finished the work, she went home is correct, because she had finished; Having finished the work, the lights were switched off is wrong. The correction is either to name the doer in the main clause or to expand the participle into a full clause.

The possessive comes before a gerund when the gerund is the object of a verb or a preposition and the doer is a pronoun or a name. We say I do not like his smoking, not I do not like him smoking, in careful writing. We say She objected to Rina's going, not to Rina going. In informal English the object form is common, but the examination usually rewards the possessive. The reason is that the gerund is a noun, and a noun is modified by a possessive, not by an object pronoun.

The infinitive after certain adjectives and nouns is a fixed pattern. Adjectives such as glad, sorry, happy, sad, eager, ready, able, unable, easy, difficult, hard and anxious take the infinitive: I am ready to go; It is difficult to say. Nouns such as ability, attempt, desire, decision, effort, need, plan, promise, refusal, willingness and wish take the infinitive: a decision to leave; a promise to help. A wrong preposition or a gerund in place of the infinitive is a common distractor.

The verb help takes either the full or the bare infinitive: She helped me to carry it, or She helped me carry it. The verbs make, let, see, hear, feel, watch and notice take the bare infinitive in the active voice, but the full infinitive in the passive: They made him work; He was made to work. This active-passive difference is asked directly, and the passive form with to is the one candidates forget.

A useful way to revise the topic is to group the verbs by pattern. Group one takes only the gerund: enjoy, avoid, mind, finish, suggest, recommend, consider, admit, deny, postpone, practise, risk, keep, dislike, imagine. Group two takes only the infinitive: want, wish, hope, expect, decide, promise, refuse, agree, offer, plan, manage, fail, afford, learn. Group three takes either with a change of meaning: stop, remember, forget, regret, try, go on, mean. Learning the groups as lists is faster than learning them one by one, and the examination rarely goes outside these lists.
The infinitive is to plus the base verb; the gerund is the ing form used as a noun; the participle is the ing or past participle form used as an adjective or in a tense.
After a preposition, use the gerund, never the infinitive.
Modals, let, make, see, hear, feel and watch take the bare infinitive.
In the passive, make, see and hear take the full infinitive with to.
Stop, remember, forget, regret, try, go on and mean change meaning with the form that follows.
A participle at the start of a sentence must describe the subject of the main clause.
Use a possessive before a gerund in careful writing.

She is interested in ___ (learn) French. The preposition in requires a gerund, so the answer is learning. The infinitive to learn would be wrong after a preposition, even though the meaning is clear. This is the single most common non-finite error in the bank.

I remember ___ (lock) the door before I left. The action of locking happened in the past, so the gerund locking is correct. If the sentence meant that the speaker must not forget a future duty, it would be I must remember to lock the door.
They made him ___ (work) late. The verb make takes the bare infinitive in the active voice, so the answer is work, without to. In the passive, the sentence becomes He was made to work late, with to.

___ (walk) down the road, I saw a snake. The participle walking describes I, the subject of the main clause, so it is correct. If the main clause were a snake was seen, the sentence would be dangling and would need to be rewritten as While I was walking down the road, I saw a snake.
Using an infinitive after a preposition.
Using to after make, let, see or hear in the active voice.
Omitting to after make, see or hear in the passive voice.
Confusing stop doing with stop to do.
Confusing remember doing with remember to do.
Leaving a participle dangling at the start of a sentence.
Using an object pronoun instead of a possessive before a gerund.

When you see a blank after a preposition or after enjoy, avoid, mind, suggest or finish, write the ing form at once. When you see a modal, let, make, see or hear, write the base form without to. Those two reflexes cover most of the questions on this topic.
as: সীমিত ক্ৰিয়া (finite verb) কৰ্তা আৰু কাল অনুসৰি সলনি হয়: I go, she goes, they went। অ-সীমিত ক্ৰিয়া (non-finite verb) সেইদৰে নসলনি, আৰু সেয়া বাক্যৰ একমাত্ৰ ক্ৰিয়া হ'ব নোৱাৰে। ইংৰাজীত তিনিটা অ-সীমিত ৰূপ আছে: infinitive, যি to ৰ লগত base verb, যেনে to write; gerund, যি ing ৰূপ বিশেষ্য হিচাপে ব্যৱহৃত, যেনে writing; আৰু participle, যি present participle writing বা past participle written। DHS আৰু DME কাৰিকৰী গ্ৰেড III পত্ৰত এই ৰূপবোৰ সংজ্ঞাৰে নহয়, verb pattern, ভুল নিৰ্ণয় আৰু বাক্য শুধৰণিৰে সোধা হয়।

Infinitive ৰ কেইবাটাও কাম আছে। ই বাক্যৰ কৰ্তা হ'ব পাৰে, যদিও ই আনুষ্ঠানিক: To err is human। ই ক্ৰিয়াৰ object হ'ব পাৰে: She wants to sing। ই উদ্দেশ্য বুজাব পাৰে: He went to the market to buy rice। ই বিশেষণৰ পিছত আহিব পাৰে: I am glad to meet you। ই বিশেষ্যৰ পিছত আহিব পাৰে: He has the ability to solve it। আৰু ই be ৰ complement হ'ব পাৰে: My aim is to serve। to ৰ অবিহনে bare infinitive modal, let, make, see, hear, feel আৰু watch ৰ পিছত আহে: She can swim; Let him go; I saw him leave।

Gerund হৈছে ing ৰূপ যি বিশেষ্যৰ কাম কৰে। ই কৰ্তা হ'ব পাৰে: Swimming is good exercise। ই object হ'ব পাৰে: She enjoys reading। ই পূৰ্বসৰ্গৰ পিছত আহিব পাৰে: He is good at painting; She insisted on coming। ই কিছুমান ক্ৰিয়াৰ পিছত আহিব পাৰে: avoid, enjoy, mind, finish, suggest, recommend, consider, admit, deny, postpone, practise, risk, keep আৰু look forward to। পূৰ্বসৰ্গৰ পিছত ক্ৰিয়া gerund হ'বই লাগে, infinitive কেতিয়াও নহয়: She is interested in learning, interested in to learn নহয়।

কিছুমান ক্ৰিয়াই দুয়ো ৰূপ লয়, কিন্তু অৰ্থ সলনি হয়। Stop doing মানে কাম এটা বন্ধ কৰা; stop to do মানে আন কাম কৰিবলৈ বিৰতি লোৱা। Remember doing মানে অতীতৰ কাম মনত পেলোৱা; remember to do মানে ভৱিষ্যতৰ কৰ্তব্য নাপাহৰা। Forget doing মানে অতীতৰ স্মৃতি হেৰুওৱা; forget to do মানে কৰ্তব্য কৰিবলৈ বিফল হোৱা। Regret doing মানে অতীতৰ বাবে অনুশোচনা; regret to do বেয়া বাতৰি জনাবলৈ ব্যৱহাৰ হয়। Try doing মানে পৰীক্ষা কৰা; try to do মানে চেষ্টা কৰা। Go on doing মানে অব্যাহত ৰখা; go on to do মানে পৰৱৰ্তী বিন্দুলৈ যোৱা। Mean doing মানে ফলস্বৰূপে জড়িত হোৱা; mean to do মানে অভিপ্ৰায় কৰা।

Present participle ৰ দুটা মূল ব্যৱহাৰ। ই be ৰ লগত continuous tense গঠন কৰে: She is writing। ই বিশেষণ হিচাপেও কাম কৰে: a running tap, a crying child, an interesting book। Past participle এ have ৰ লগত perfect tense আৰু be ৰ লগত passive গঠন কৰে: She has written; The letter was written। ই বিশেষণ হিচাপেও কাম কৰে: a broken window, a written test, a tired traveller। an interesting book আৰু an interested reader ৰ পাৰ্থক্য হৈছে present participle, যি অনুভৱ সৃষ্টি কৰে, আৰু past participle, যি অনুভৱ গ্ৰহণ কৰে, তাৰ পাৰ্থক্য।

Dangling participle এটা সাধাৰণ ভুল। বাক্যৰ আৰম্ভণিত থকা participle এ মূল উপবাক্যৰ কৰ্তাক বৰ্ণনা কৰিব লাগে। Walking down the road, I saw a snake শুদ্ধ, কাৰণ মই খোজ কাঢ়ি আছিলোঁ। Walking down the road, a snake was seen ভুল, কাৰণ সাপে খোজ কঢ়া নাছিল। একেই নিয়ম perfect participle ৰ বাবেও: Having finished the work, she went home শুদ্ধ, কাৰণ তাই কাম শেষ কৰিছিল; Having finished the work, the lights were switched off ভুল। শুধৰণি হৈছে মূল উপবাক্যত কৰ্তা নাম দিয়া, বা participle ক সম্পূৰ্ণ উপবাক্যলৈ বঢ়াই দিয়া।

Gerund ৰ আগত possessive আহে যেতিয়া gerund ক্ৰিয়া বা পূৰ্বসৰ্গৰ object হয় আৰু কৰ্তা সৰ্বনাম বা নাম হয়। যতনশীল লিখাত আমি I do not like his smoking লিখোঁ, I do not like him smoking নহয়। আমি She objected to Rina's going লিখোঁ, to Rina going নহয়। অনানুষ্ঠানিক ইংৰাজীত object form সাধাৰণ, কিন্তু পৰীক্ষাই সাধাৰণতে possessive ক পুৰস্কৃত কৰে। কাৰণ gerund এটা বিশেষ্য, আৰু বিশেষ্যক possessive ৰে বৰ্ণনা কৰা হয়, object pronoun ৰে নহয়।

কিছুমান বিশেষণ আৰু বিশেষ্যৰ পিছত infinitive এটা নিৰ্দিষ্ট আৰ্হি। Glad, sorry, happy, sad, eager, ready, able, unable, easy, difficult, hard, anxious যেনে বিশেষণে infinitive লয়: I am ready to go; It is difficult to say। Ability, attempt, desire, decision, effort, need, plan, promise, refusal, willingness, wish যেনে বিশেষ্যই infinitive লয়: a decision to leave; a promise to help। ভুল পূৰ্বসৰ্গ বা infinitive ৰ ঠাইত gerund এটা সাধাৰণ বিভ্ৰান্তিকৰ বিকল্প।

Help ক্ৰিয়াই পূৰ্ণ বা bare infinitive দুয়োটা লয়: She helped me to carry it, বা She helped me carry it। Make, let, see, hear, feel, watch, notice এ active voice ত bare infinitive লয়, কিন্তু passive ত পূৰ্ণ infinitive লয়: They made him work; He was made to work। এই active-passive পাৰ্থক্য প্ৰত্যক্ষভাৱে সোধা হয়, আৰু passive ত to থকা ৰূপটোৱেই প্ৰাৰ্থীয়ে পাহৰে।

বিষয়টো পুনৰালোচনাৰ এটা সহজ উপায় হৈছে ক্ৰিয়াবোৰ আৰ্হি অনুসৰি গোট কৰা। প্ৰথম গোটে কেৱল gerund লয়: enjoy, avoid, mind, finish, suggest, recommend, consider, admit, deny, postpone, practise, risk, keep, dislike, imagine। দ্বিতীয় গোটে কেৱল infinitive লয়: want, wish, hope, expect, decide, promise, refuse, agree, offer, plan, manage, fail, afford, learn। তৃতীয় গোটে অৰ্থ সলনি হ'লে দুয়োটা লয়: stop, remember, forget, regret, try, go on, mean। গোটবোৰ তালিকা হিচাপে শিকা এটা এটাকৈ শিকাতকৈ দ্ৰুত, আৰু পৰীক্ষাই বিৰলভাৱে এই তালিকাৰ বাহিৰলৈ যায়।

Perfect gerund আৰু passive gerund ৰ ৰূপও চিনি ৰাখিব লাগে। Having finished the work, she left ত having finished হৈছে perfect participle, যি কামটো আগতে সম্পূৰ্ণ হোৱা দেখুৱায়। I remember having met him ত having met হৈছে perfect gerund, যি আগৰ অভিজ্ঞতা মনত পেলোৱা বুজায়। Passive gerund being + past participle: She hates being praised। Passive infinitive to be + past participle: She wants to be praised। Perfect infinitive to have + past participle: He seems to have forgotten। এই ৰূপবোৰ প্ৰায়ে tense আৰু voice ৰ প্ৰশ্নৰ সৈতে মিলি আহে, আৰু ৰূপটো ভুল কৰিলে অৰ্থই সলনি হয়।
Infinitive হৈছে to + base verb; gerund হৈছে বিশেষ্য হিচাপে ব্যৱহৃত ing ৰূপ; participle হৈছে tense বা বিশেষণত ব্যৱহৃত ing বা past participle ৰূপ।
পূৰ্বসৰ্গৰ পিছত gerund, infinitive কেতিয়াও নহয়।
Modal, let, make, see, hear, feel, watch এ bare infinitive লয়।
Passive ত make, see, hear এ to ৰে পূৰ্ণ infinitive লয়।
Stop, remember, forget, regret, try, go on, mean ৰ অৰ্থ পৰৱৰ্তী ৰূপৰ ওপৰত নিৰ্ভৰ কৰে।
বাক্যৰ আৰম্ভণিত থকা participle এ মূল উপবাক্যৰ কৰ্তাক বৰ্ণনা কৰিব লাগে।
যতনশীল লিখাত gerund ৰ আগত possessive ব্যৱহাৰ কৰক।
Perfect gerund ৰ ৰূপ having + past participle আৰু passive gerund ৰ ৰূপ being + past participle, দুয়োটা চিনি ৰাখক।
She is interested in ___ (learn) French। পূৰ্বসৰ্গ in এ gerund বিচাৰে, গতিকে উত্তৰ learning। to learn ভুল, কাৰণ পূৰ্বসৰ্গৰ পিছত infinitive নাহে। এইটোৱেই প্ৰশ্নগোটৰ আটাইতকৈ সাধাৰণ non-finite ভুল।

I remember ___ (lock) the door before I left। তলা দিয়া কাম অতীতত হৈছিল, গতিকে gerund locking শুদ্ধ। যদি বাক্যই ভৱিষ্যতৰ কৰ্তব্য নাপাহৰা বুজালেহেঁতেন, তেন্তে I must remember to lock the door হ'লহেঁতেন।
They made him ___ (work) late। Make এ active voice ত bare infinitive লয়, গতিকে উত্তৰ work, to ৰ অবিহনে। Passive ত বাক্যটো He was made to work late হয়, to ৰ সৈতে।

___ (walk) down the road, I saw a snake। Participle walking এ I, মূল উপবাক্যৰ কৰ্তাক বৰ্ণনা কৰে, গতিকে শুদ্ধ। যদি মূল উপবাক্য a snake was seen হ'লহেঁতেন, বাক্যটো dangling হ'লহেঁতেন আৰু While I was walking down the road, I saw a snake হিচাপে পুনৰ লিখিব লাগিলেহেঁতেন।
Active voice ত make, let, see, hear ৰ পিছত to ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা।
Passive voice ত make, see, hear ৰ পিছত to বাদ দিয়া।
stop doing আৰু stop to do ৰ মাজত বিভ্ৰান্ত হোৱা।
remember doing আৰু remember to do ৰ মাজত বিভ্ৰান্ত হোৱা।
Gerund ৰ আগত object pronoun ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা, possessive ৰ সলনি।

পূৰ্বসৰ্গৰ পিছত বা enjoy, avoid, mind, suggest, finish ৰ পিছত ৰিক্ত স্থান দেখিলে লগে লগে ing ৰূপ লিখক। Modal, let, make, see বা hear দেখিলে to ৰ অবিহনে base form লিখক। এই দুটা অভ্যাসেই এই বিষয়ৰ বেছিভাগ প্ৰশ্ন সামৰি লয়, আৰু প্ৰতিটো ভুলৰ পিছত কোনটো গোটৰ ক্ৰিয়া আছিল তাক লিখি ৰাখিলে পুনৰাবৃত্তি কমি যায়।

en: A preposition is a word that shows the relation between a noun or a pronoun and another word in the sentence, and it almost always has an object. In the sentence the book is on the table, the word on shows the relation between the book and the table, and table is the object of the preposition. The DHS & DME Technical Grade III paper asks prepositions more often than almost any other single grammar point, both in fill in the blanks and in error spotting, and the reason is simple: the same verb or adjective may take different prepositions in different senses, and there is no rule that predicts the choice with certainty. The only dependable method is to learn each preposition with the word it follows.

Prepositions of place answer the question where. In is used for a large area or an enclosed space, so that we live in Assam and the pen is in the box. At is used for a point or a small place, so that we wait at the gate and the train stops at the station. On is used for a surface, so that the cup is on the table and the picture hangs on the wall. Over means above and across, as in the plane flew over the hill, and under means below, as in the cat is under the chair. Between is used for two things and among for more than two, so that we divide the money between the two brothers and among the four children.

Prepositions of time follow their own set of rules. At is used for a point of time, as in at five o clock and at noon. On is used for a day or a date, as in on Monday and on the fifth of May. In is used for a month, a season, a year or a long period, as in in June, in winter and in 1990. Since is used with a point of time from which something began, as in since morning and since 2015, while for is used with a length of time, as in for two hours and for ten years. During means through the whole of a period, as in during the war, and by means not later than, as in finish it by Monday.

Prepositions of movement and direction include to, into, onto, towards, through, across, along and past. To shows the goal of a movement, as in he went to Delhi. Into shows movement from outside to inside, as in she walked into the room. Onto shows movement to a surface. Through means from one side to the other inside something, as in the train went through the tunnel, while across means from one side to the other on a surface, as in he swam across the river. Along means following the length of something, as in we walked along the road.

Certain verbs are followed by fixed prepositions and must be learnt as single units. We listen to music, wait for a bus, look at a picture, look for a lost key, look after a child and look into a matter. We consist of parts, deal in goods, deal with a person, depend on someone, insist on a thing, and comply with a rule. We agree with a person and agree to a proposal, we apologise for a mistake and apologise to a person, and we congratulate a person on a success. These verb-plus-preposition combinations are the single richest source of fill in the blank questions.

Adjectives, too, take fixed prepositions. We are afraid of dogs, good at mathematics, bad at singing, angry with a person and angry at a thing, angry about an event, proud of a child, fond of sweets, jealous of a rival, sorry for a mistake, sorry about an event, confident of success, capable of doing work, famous for a quality, known for honesty, married to a person, engaged to a person, and addicted to a habit. We are also afraid of a thing, aware of a danger, ashamed of a fault, accused of a crime, deprived of a right, and tired of a routine. Each of these pairs is worth writing on a card.

Nouns, as well, may be followed by a fixed preposition. We have a need for something, a demand for a thing, a reason for an act, a cause of a problem, a solution to a difficulty, a key to a lock, a reply to a letter, an answer to a question, an affection for a person, and a taste for music. A rise in price, a fall in temperature, an increase in population and a decrease in rainfall are all common in examination sentences. Learning a noun together with its preposition prevents the error that comes from translating directly from Assamese.

The preposition is also used with certain set phrases that must be learnt whole. We say in time meaning before the deadline and on time meaning at the fixed time. We say at present, in future, in the end meaning finally, and at the end meaning at the last point. We say on foot, by bus, by train, by air, in a car and on a bicycle. We say at home, at work, in bed, on the way, in the morning, on Sunday morning, and at night. These phrases are fixed, and changing one word makes the phrase wrong.

The most frequent error is the use of a wrong preposition with a verb or an adjective, and it comes from two sources. The first is the influence of the mother tongue, which leads a candidate to write married with instead of married to, or discuss about instead of discuss. The second is the confusion between two prepositions that look alike, such as since and for, between and among, on and in, and by and with. When a sentence is read with the suspect preposition removed and the correct question of place, time or manner is asked, the right preposition usually becomes clear.

Some verbs take no preposition at all, and adding one is a common error. We discuss a matter, not discuss about a matter; we enter a room, not enter into a room; we reach a place, not reach at a place; we order a meal, not order for a meal; and we return home, not return to home. Conversely, some verbs need a preposition that candidates often drop, as in listen to music and reply to a letter. A short list of these two groups is worth memorising, because each one turns up regularly in the error-spotting section.

A preposition is normally followed by a noun, a pronoun in the objective case, or a gerund. We say he is good at painting and not he is good at paint, and we say she is afraid of falling and not she is afraid of fall. A pronoun after a preposition takes the objective form, so that we write between you and me and not between you and I. These two rules explain a large share of the questions on the chapter, and they are easy to apply once they are known.

Some prepositions are used to show relations other than place and time. Of shows possession or connection, as in the roof of the house. By is used for the doer in the passive voice, as in the letter was written by him. With is used for an instrument, as in he cut the rope with a knife. For shows purpose or benefit, as in this gift is for you. Without means in the absence of, as in he came without a coat. About and on are both used for a subject, though on suggests a more formal treatment.

A practical method for the examination is to read the whole sentence before filling the blank, because the preposition is decided by the word it follows rather than by the blank alone. If the blank follows an adjective, recall the adjective-preposition pair; if it follows a verb, recall the verb-preposition pair; if it follows a noun, recall the noun-preposition pair. In error spotting, check every preposition in the sentence against the word before it. With a card of the common pairs revised for a week, this chapter becomes one of the easiest places to gain marks.
In a large area, at a point, on a surface, between two, among more than two.
At a time, on a day, in a month or year, since a point of time, for a length of time.
Listen to, wait for, look after, depend on, insist on, comply with.
Afraid of, good at, angry with a person, angry at a thing, married to, addicted to.
A reason for, a cause of, a solution to, a key to, a reply to.
Discuss a matter, enter a room, reach a place and order a meal take no preposition.
A preposition is followed by a noun, an objective pronoun or a gerund.
In time means before the deadline and on time means at the fixed time.
Q: Why is married with wrong? A: The adjective married takes the preposition to, so the correct phrase is married to a person, never married with.
Q: What is the difference between since and for? A: Since is used with a point of time, as in since 2015, while for is used with a length of time, as in for five years.
Q. Work hard ___ you should fail. (A) lest (B) unless (C) until (D) if The correct choice is lest. 'Lest' is followed by 'should' and means 'for fear that'.
Q. He not only sings ___ dances. (A) and (B) but also (C) or (D) nor The correct choice is but also. 'Not only ... but also' is the correct correlative pair.
Q. He is so tired ___ he cannot walk. (A) so (B) as (C) that (D) than The correct choice is that. 'So ... that' is the correct correlative pair.
Q. Find the error: 'He is senior than me.' (A) He is (B) senior (C) than (D) me The correct choice is than. 'Senior' is followed by 'to', not 'than'.

In the DHS & DME Technical Grade III paper this topic appears inside error spotting, fill in the blanks and sentence correction rather than as a definition. Practise the bank with the rule in mind, and note which rule each wrong option breaks.
as: পূৰ্বসৰ্গ হৈছে এনে এটা শব্দ যি বাক্যত এটা বিশেষ্য বা সৰ্বনাম আৰু আন এটা শব্দৰ মাজৰ সম্পৰ্ক দেখুৱায়, আৰু ইয়াৰ প্ৰায় সদায় এটা object থাকে। the book is on the table বাক্যত on শব্দই book আৰু table ৰ মাজৰ সম্পৰ্ক দেখুৱায়, আৰু table হৈছে পূৰ্বসৰ্গৰ object। DHS & DME Technical Grade III গ্ৰেড III পত্ৰই প্ৰায় যিকোনো এটা ব্যাকৰণ বিন্দুতকৈ পূৰ্বসৰ্গ বেছি সোধে, ৰিক্ত স্থান পূৰণ আৰু ভুল নিৰ্ণয় দুয়োটাৰে, আৰু কাৰণটো সৰল: একে ক্ৰিয়া বা বিশেষণে ভিন্ন অৰ্থত ভিন্ন পূৰ্বসৰ্গ লয়, আৰু বাচনি নিশ্চিতভাৱে ক'ব পৰা কোনো নিয়ম নাই। একমাত্ৰ নিৰ্ভৰযোগ্য পদ্ধতি হ'ল প্ৰতিটো পূৰ্বসৰ্গ তাৰ লগত অহা শব্দৰ সৈতে শিকা।

স্থানৰ পূৰ্বসৰ্গই ক'ত — এই প্ৰশ্নৰ উত্তৰ দিয়ে। In ডাঙৰ অঞ্চল বা আবদ্ধ ঠাইৰ বাবে ব্যৱহাৰ হয়, গতিকে we live in Assam আৰু the pen is in the box। At এটা বিন্দু বা সৰু ঠাইৰ বাবে, গতিকে we wait at the gate আৰু the train stops at the station। On পৃষ্ঠৰ বাবে, গতিকে the cup is on the table আৰু the picture hangs on the wall। Over মানে ওপৰত আৰু সিটো কাষলৈ, যেনে the plane flew over the hill, আৰু under মানে তলত, যেনে the cat is under the chair। Between দুইৰ বাবে আৰু among দুইতকৈ বেছিৰ বাবে, গতিকে divide the money between the two brothers আৰু among the four children।

সময়ৰ পূৰ্বসৰ্গৰ নিজা নিয়ম। At এটা সময়ৰ বিন্দুৰ বাবে, যেনে at five o clock আৰু at noon। On এটা দিন বা তাৰিখৰ বাবে, যেনে on Monday আৰু on the fifth of May। In এটা মাহ, ঋতু, বছৰ বা দীঘল কালৰ বাবে, যেনে in June, in winter আৰু in 1990। Since এটা সময়ৰ বিন্দুৰ সৈতে য'ৰপৰা কিবা আৰম্ভ হৈছিল, যেনে since morning আৰু since 2015, আনহাতে for এটা সময়ৰ দৈৰ্ঘ্যৰ সৈতে, যেনে for two hours আৰু for ten years। During মানে গোটেই সময়জুৰি, যেনে during the war, আৰু by মানে তাতকৈ পিছত নহয়, যেনে finish it by Monday।

গতি আৰু দিশৰ পূৰ্বসৰ্গৰ ভিতৰত to, into, onto, towards, through, across, along আৰু past পৰে। To এটা গতিৰ লক্ষ্য দেখুৱায়, যেনে he went to Delhi। Into বাহিৰৰ পৰা ভিতৰলৈ গতি দেখুৱায়, যেনে she walked into the room। Onto পৃষ্ঠলৈ গতি দেখুৱায়। Through মানে কিবাৰ ভিতৰেদি এটা কাষৰ পৰা আন কাষলৈ, যেনে the train went through the tunnel, আনহাতে across মানে পৃষ্ঠত এটা কাষৰ পৰা আন কাষলৈ, যেনে he swam across the river। Along মানে কিবাৰ দীঘে দীঘে, যেনে we walked along the road।

কিছুমান ক্ৰিয়াৰ পিছত নিৰ্দিষ্ট পূৰ্বসৰ্গ আহে আৰু ইহঁতক এটা একক হিচাপে শিকিব লাগে। আমি listen to music, wait for a bus, look at a picture, look for a lost key, look after a child আৰু look into a matter লিখোঁ। আমি consist of parts, deal in goods, deal with a person, depend on someone, insist on a thing, আৰু comply with a rule লিখোঁ। আমি agree with a person আৰু agree to a proposal, apologise for a mistake আৰু apologise to a person, আৰু congratulate a person on a success লিখোঁ। ক্ৰিয়া-পূৰ্বসৰ্গৰ এই যোৰবোৰ ৰিক্ত স্থান পূৰণৰ প্ৰশ্নৰ সৰ্বাধিক উৎস।

বিশেষণেও নিৰ্দিষ্ট পূৰ্বসৰ্গ লয়। আমি afraid of dogs, good at mathematics, bad at singing, angry with a person আৰু angry at a thing, angry about an event, proud of a child, fond of sweets, jealous of a rival, sorry for a mistake, sorry about an event, confident of success, capable of doing work, famous for a quality, known for honesty, married to a person, engaged to a person, আৰু addicted to a habit লিখোঁ। আমি afraid of a thing, aware of a danger, ashamed of a fault, accused of a crime, deprived of a right, আৰু tired of a routineও লিখোঁ। এই যোৰবোৰৰ প্ৰতিটো এখন কাৰ্ডত লিখাৰ যোগ্য।

বিশেষ্যৰ পিছতো নিৰ্দিষ্ট পূৰ্বসৰ্গ আহিব পাৰে। আমি a need for something, a demand for a thing, a reason for an act, a cause of a problem, a solution to a difficulty, a key to a lock, a reply to a letter, an answer to a question, an affection for a person, আৰু a taste for music লিখোঁ। a rise in price, a fall in temperature, an increase in population আৰু a decrease in rainfall — এইবোৰ পৰীক্ষাৰ বাক্যত সাধাৰণ। বিশেষ্যক তাৰ পূৰ্বসৰ্গৰ সৈতে একেলগে শিকিলে অসমীয়াৰ পৰা পোনপটীয়াকৈ অনুবাদ কৰি কৰা ভুল ৰোধ হয়।

কিছুমান নিৰ্দিষ্ট বাক্যাংশতো পূৰ্বসৰ্গ ব্যৱহাৰ হয়, যিবোৰ গোটেইটো শিকিব লাগে। আমি in time মানে সময়সীমাৰ আগতে আৰু on time মানে নিৰ্ধাৰিত সময়ত লিখোঁ। আমি at present, in future, in the end মানে শেষত, আৰু at the end মানে শেষ বিন্দুত লিখোঁ। আমি on foot, by bus, by train, by air, in a car আৰু on a bicycle লিখোঁ। আমি at home, at work, in bed, on the way, in the morning, on Sunday morning, আৰু at night লিখোঁ। এই বাক্যাংশবোৰ স্থিৰ, এটা শব্দ সলালে বাক্যাংশটো ভুল হয়।

সৰ্বাধিক বাৰে হোৱা ভুল হৈছে ক্ৰিয়া বা বিশেষণৰ সৈতে ভুল পূৰ্বসৰ্গ ব্যৱহাৰ কৰা, আৰু ইয়াৰ দুটা উৎস। প্ৰথমটো হ'ল মাতৃভাষাৰ প্ৰভাৱ, যাৰ ফলত প্ৰাৰ্থীয়ে married to ৰ সলনি married with, বা discuss ৰ সলনি discuss about লিখে। দ্বিতীয়টো হ'ল একে দেখুৱা দুটা পূৰ্বসৰ্গৰ মাজত বিভ্ৰম, যেনে since আৰু for, between আৰু among, on আৰু in, আৰু by আৰু with। সন্দেহজনক পূৰ্বসৰ্গ বাদ দি বাক্যটো পঢ়ি স্থান, সময় বা ধৰণৰ শুদ্ধ প্ৰশ্ন কৰিলে শুদ্ধ পূৰ্বসৰ্গ সাধাৰণতে স্পষ্ট হৈ পৰে।

কিছুমান ক্ৰিয়াই কোনো পূৰ্বসৰ্গ নলয়, আৰু এটা যোগ কৰাটো সাধাৰণ ভুল। আমি discuss a matter লিখোঁ, discuss about a matter নহয়; enter a room লিখোঁ, enter into a room নহয়; reach a place লিখোঁ, reach at a place নহয়; order a meal লিখোঁ, order for a meal নহয়; আৰু return home লিখোঁ, return to home নহয়। ওলোটাকৈ, কিছুমান ক্ৰিয়াৰ প্ৰয়োজনীয় পূৰ্বসৰ্গ প্ৰাৰ্থীয়ে প্ৰায়ে বাদ দিয়ে, যেনে listen to music আৰু reply to a letter। এই দুই গোটৰ এটা চুটি তালিকা মনত ৰখাৰ যোগ্য, কাৰণ প্ৰতিটো নিয়মিতভাৱে ভুল নিৰ্ণয় অংশত ওলায়।

পূৰ্বসৰ্গৰ পিছত সাধাৰণতে এটা বিশেষ্য, কৰ্ম কাৰকৰ সৰ্বনাম, বা এটা gerund আহে। আমি he is good at painting লিখোঁ, he is good at paint নহয়; আৰু she is afraid of falling লিখোঁ, she is afraid of fall নহয়। পূৰ্বসৰ্গৰ পিছৰ সৰ্বনামে কৰ্ম ৰূপ লয়, গতিকে between you and me লিখোঁ, between you and I নহয়। এই দুটা নিয়মেই অধ্যায়ৰ প্ৰশ্নৰ এটা ডাঙৰ অংশ ব্যাখ্যা কৰে, আৰু জনা হ'লে প্ৰয়োগ কৰা সহজ।

কিছুমান পূৰ্বসৰ্গ স্থান আৰু সময়ৰ বাহিৰে আন সম্পৰ্কও দেখুৱায়। Of মালিকী বা সম্পৰ্ক দেখুৱায়, যেনে the roof of the house। By passive voice ত কৰ্তাৰ বাবে ব্যৱহাৰ হয়, যেনে the letter was written by him। With যন্ত্ৰৰ বাবে ব্যৱহাৰ হয়, যেনে he cut the rope with a knife। For উদ্দেশ্য বা লাভৰ বাবে, যেনে this gift is for you। Without মানে অবিহনে, যেনে he came without a coat। About আৰু on দুয়োটা বিষয়ৰ বাবে, যদিও on এ বেছি আনুষ্ঠানিক প্ৰকাশ বুজায়।

পৰীক্ষাৰ বাবে এটা ব্যৱহৃত পদ্ধতি হ'ল ৰিক্ত স্থান পূৰণ কৰাৰ আগতে গোটেই বাক্যটো পঢ়া, কাৰণ পূৰ্বসৰ্গ কেৱল ৰিক্ত স্থানৰ দ্বাৰা নহয়, তাৰ আগৰ শব্দৰ দ্বাৰাহে নিৰ্ণয় হয়। ৰিক্ত স্থান যদি বিশেষণৰ পিছত, তেন্তে বিশেষণ-পূৰ্বসৰ্গ যোৰা মনত পেলাওক; যদি ক্ৰিয়াৰ পিছত, তেন্তে ক্ৰিয়া-পূৰ্বসৰ্গ যোৰা; যদি বিশেষ্যৰ পিছত, তেন্তে বিশেষ্য-পূৰ্বসৰ্গ যোৰা। ভুল নিৰ্ণয়ত বাক্যৰ প্ৰতিটো পূৰ্বসৰ্গ তাৰ আগৰ শব্দৰ সৈতে মিলাই চাওক। সাধাৰণ যোৰবোৰৰ এটা কাৰ্ড এসপ্তাহ পুনৰালোচনা কৰিলে এই অধ্যায় নম্বৰ পোৱাৰ আটাইতকৈ সহজ ঠাই হৈ পৰে।
ডাঙৰ অঞ্চলত in, বিন্দুত at, পৃষ্ঠত on, দুইত between, দুইতকৈ বেছিত among।
সময়ৰ বিন্দুত at, দিনত on, মাহ বা বছৰত in, সময়ৰ বিন্দুৰপৰা since, সময়ৰ দৈৰ্ঘ্যত for।
Listen to, wait for, look after, depend on, insist on, comply with।
Afraid of, good at, angry with a person, angry at a thing, married to, addicted to।
A reason for, a cause of, a solution to, a key to, a reply to।
Discuss a matter, enter a room, reach a place আৰু order a meal য়ে কোনো পূৰ্বসৰ্গ নলয়।
পূৰ্বসৰ্গৰ পিছত বিশেষ্য, কৰ্ম সৰ্বনাম বা gerund আহে।
In time মানে সময়সীমাৰ আগতে আৰু on time মানে নিৰ্ধাৰিত সময়ত।
প্ৰশ্ন: married with কিয় ভুল? উত্তৰ: বিশেষণ married য়ে to পূৰ্বসৰ্গ লয়, গতিকে শুদ্ধ বাক্যাংশ married to a person, married with কেতিয়াও নহয়।
প্ৰশ্ন: since আৰু for ৰ মাজত পাৰ্থক্য কি? উত্তৰ: Since এটা সময়ৰ বিন্দুৰ সৈতে ব্যৱহাৰ হয়, যেনে since 2015; আনহাতে for এটা সময়ৰ দৈৰ্ঘ্যৰ সৈতে, যেনে for five years।
প্ৰশ্ন: between you and I কিয় ভুল? উত্তৰ: পূৰ্বসৰ্গই কৰ্ম কাৰক লয়, গতিকে শুদ্ধ ৰূপ between you and me।
প্ৰশ্ন: কোনবোৰ শব্দৰ পিছত পূৰ্বসৰ্গ নাহে? উত্তৰ: Discuss, enter, reach, order আৰু return home য়ে পূৰ্বসৰ্গ নলয়, গতিকে discuss the matter লিখোঁ, discuss about the matter নহয়।

কৰ্তা-ক্ৰিয়াৰ মিল হৈছে সেই নিয়ম যে ক্ৰিয়াৱে কৰ্তাৰ সংখ্যা আৰু পুৰুষৰ সৈতে মিলিব লাগে। একবচন কৰ্তাই একবচন ক্ৰিয়া লয় আৰু বহুবচন কৰ্তাই বহুবচন ক্ৰিয়া লয়। এইটো সৰল শুনায়, আৰু চুটি বাক্যত সৰলো, কিন্তু পৰীক্ষাই প্ৰকৃত কৰ্তাক বাক্যাংশ, উপবাক্য আৰু বন্ধনীৰ প্ৰকাশৰ পিছত লুকুৱাই ৰাখে, আৰু তেতিয়া নিয়মটো মনত ৰখাৰ নহয়, সাৱধানে পঢ়াৰ পৰীক্ষা হৈ পৰে। DHS & DME Technical Grade III গ্ৰেড III পত্ৰত এই অধ্যায় ভুল নিৰ্ণয়, ৰিক্ত স্থান পূৰণ আৰু বাক্য শুধৰণিত ওলায়, আৰু প্ৰকৃত কৰ্তা বিচাৰি পালে ইয়াৰ ভুলবোৰ বিচাৰি পোৱা আটাইতকৈ সহজ।

প্ৰথম আৰু আটাইতকৈ কামৰ পদ্ধতি হ'ল ক্ৰিয়া চোৱাৰ আগতে প্ৰকৃত কৰ্তা বিচৰা। the colour of the walls is white বাক্যত ক্ৰিয়াৱে walls ৰ সৈতে নহয়, colour ৰ সৈতে মিলিব লাগে, গতিকে is শুদ্ধ। the boy with the two dogs was walking বাক্যত ক্ৰিয়া boy ৰ সৈতে মিলে, গতিকে was শুদ্ধ। with, along with, together with, as well as, in addition to, besides, including বা accompanied by ৰে আৰম্ভ হোৱা বাক্যাংশই কৰ্তাৰ সংখ্যা সলনি নকৰে, আৰু এইটো পাহৰাই এই অধ্যায়ৰ সৰ্বাধিক সাধাৰণ ভুল।
এই প্ৰশ্নগোটৰ পৰা সমাধান কৰা প্ৰশ্ন
প্ৰ. কঠোৰ পৰিশ্ৰম কৰা, নহ'লে তুমি অনুত্তীৰ্ণ হ'বা। (A) lest (B) unless (C) until (D) if শুদ্ধ উত্তৰ lest। 'lest' ৰ পিছত 'should' আহে আৰু ই 'ভয়ত যাতে' বুজায়।
প্ৰ. তেওঁ কেৱল গান নকৰে, নৃত্যও কৰে। (A) and (B) but also (C) or (D) nor শুদ্ধ উত্তৰ but also। 'not only ... but also' হৈছে শুদ্ধ correlative যুগল।
প্ৰ. তেওঁ ইমান ভাগৰুৱা যে খোজ কাঢ়িব নোৱাৰে। (A) so (B) as (C) that (D) than শুদ্ধ উত্তৰ that। 'so ... that' হৈছে শুদ্ধ correlative যুগল।
প্ৰ. ভুল উলিয়াওক: 'He is senior than me.' (A) He is (B) senior (C) than (D) me শুদ্ধ উত্তৰ than। 'senior' ৰ পিছত 'than' নহয়, 'to' আহে।

DHS আৰু DME কাৰিকৰী গ্ৰেড III পত্ৰত এই বিষয়টো সংজ্ঞা হিচাপে নহয়, ভুল নিৰ্ণয়, ৰিক্ত স্থান পূৰণ আৰু বাক্য শুধৰণিত আহে। নিয়ম মনত ৰাখি প্ৰশ্নগোটটো অভ্যাস কৰক, আৰু প্ৰতিটো ভুল বিকল্পে কোনটো নিয়ম ভাঙে তাক লিখি ৰাখক।

en: A synonym is a word that has nearly the same meaning as another word. In the DHS & DME Technical Grade III paper the question gives one word and asks the candidate to choose, from four options, the one closest in sense to it. This chapter rewards a wide reading vocabulary more than any rule, but it also rewards a method, and a candidate who follows a method will beat a candidate who merely recognises a few words. The method has three parts: read the given word in a phrase, decide its exact shade of meaning, and then test each option in the same phrase.

The first step is to give the given word a context, because most words have more than one sense. The word bright means shining in bright sunlight, clever in a bright student, and cheerful in a bright smile. The word fair means just in a fair decision, beautiful in a fair lady, and average in a fair result. The word light means not heavy, not dark, and easy. When the examiner chooses a word with several senses, the option that fits the most common sense is usually the intended answer, and the candidate must decide the sense from the options offered.

The second step is to judge the shade of meaning, because synonyms are rarely identical. Anger, rage, fury and wrath all name the same feeling, but they differ in strength, and wrath suggests a solemn and lasting anger.
